- [~] **F-253** Particle wall film (Nusselt thickness, mass conservation)
  - depends on: F-128, F-056
  - acceptance: Wall film: a laminar film fed by impinging parcels on an inclined wall reaches the Nusselt thickness
    derived in the ADR, delta = (3 mu Gamma / (rho^2 g sin(theta)))^(1/3) with Gamma the mass flow per unit width,
    within 5 percent at a station away from the feed, at a film Reynolds number inside the laminar range registered in
    the ADR; film + airborne + escaped parcel mass conserved to 1e-10 relative.
    - Out of scope: comparison with measured data beyond the stated data set, particle reactions, discrete-element
      coupling.
  - note: Split from F-245 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Size M.

      wall patches (rcfd_particles::film; the optional table particles.film with enabled, patches and viscosity, absent
      from every existing case). A parcel that reaches it is absorbed (state film). The film moves down the wall with
      the lubrication velocity rho h^2 g_t/(3 mu) by donor-cell fluxes under a Courant limit on the kinematic wave, and
      drains at open edges. On a 30-degree incline fed by four parcel streams at Re_f = 4 Gamma/mu = 2 (laminar range 0
      to 30, long-wave threshold 5.77 at 30 degrees), the station six rows below the feed is within 2.6e-15 of the
      Nusselt thickness as a window average and 1.7e-11 at 20 s (limit 5 percent); injected = airborne + deposited +
      escaped + stuck + film + drained to 6.1e-13 (limit 1e-10). The case tree, with gravity tilted instead of the mesh,
      gives 1.7e-11 and equals the library bit for bit. Runs without the film are unchanged bit for bit (records R1 and
      R2, made on main before the code). The first run of the tree checks stopped at a set-up defect of case K (frozen
      flow needs energy.enabled), corrected by amendment 1 before the corrected run; the tests on the registered K stay
      ignored.
    - Open: gas buoyancy is left out of the film so that its steady state is the roadmap formula (ADR 0192 Q2); gas
      shear (Q3) and splash or rebound at impact (Q4) are not delivered.
    - USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0192 decision record): stays PARTIAL (Q1, not closed yet); gas buoyancy and gas

    dynamic_mesh motion with rigid or smoothing deformation (the ALE step of ADR 0090), and dynamic_mesh.deformation =
    layering runs ADR 0090's planar layer stack of a piston on the new generator mesh.generator = box_3d (thresholds 0.4
    and 1.6 of lx / nx, no key); no new key, defaults and the incompressible checks unchanged; invalid settings give
    located errors (E1 to E13; E8 and E2 also through rcfd validate, E8 with its line number), and a piston driven
    through the last static plane stops the run with a dynamic_mesh: message; ADR 0090's piston P (9191 steps, 24
    removals and 24 additions), a smoothed piston with a static pressure outlet and a rigidly moving uniform flow give
    the same bits through the tree as through library calls (limit 1e-12), and rcfd run gives the reports of the
    in-process run; ADR 0090's limits hold on the tree run (p V^gamma 1.5e-5 at full compression and 3.4e-5 after the
    stroke against 2e-2, mass drift 5.4e-13 against 1e-12); fixed-mesh compressible runs are bit-identical to main (D0),
    baseline hashes and H1 unedited. Open after ADR 0191: the wiring of F-257 and F-258, layer thresholds as keys (Q1),
    the Studio's cell estimate for box_3d (Q4, F-293). USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0191 decision record): stays
    PARTIAL (Q3, not closed yet); inverse-volume smoothing is the new item F-290 (Q2 (b)); box_3d in the Studio's lists
    follows the maintainer's Studio worktree (Q4 (a), F-293); Q1 was not asked. The SV202 message observed in addendum 1
    is recorded under F-240. DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0257, 2026-11-12; ADR 0207 Q1 (a) and ADR 0213 Q1 (a) taken on
    the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): the tree runs the library work of F-257 and F-258.
    Characteristic compressible conditions may be on patches that move (ADR 0191's refusal E5 lifted; its test L is an
    ignored record, the new test L2 asserts the new behaviour); the optional table [mesh.box_3d] section = "box"
    (default), "rectangles" or "triangles" builds box_3d as the extruded layer stack, so layering runs on prism layers
    and, with piso / pimple, on the incompressible path (velocity, pressure and face flux remapped at every layer
    change); the optional table [dynamic_mesh.compressible] time_step = "mesh_speed" takes the mesh-speed step (default
    "absolute", the step of ADR 0191). Both tables are optional tables: a case that does not write them keeps its text,
    hash and results (H1, baseline hashes and the goldens unedited; ADR 0191's runs and D0 hashes unchanged; time_step =
    "absolute" equals no table bit for bit). Tree runs equal library runs with the same bits (limit 1e-12): a uniform
    flow with total inlet, pressure outlet, far field and non-reflecting outlet on moving faces (70 steps, uniform to
    8.6e-15), the Mach 0.2 piston with the mesh-speed step (613 steps against 625), ADR 0090's piston on prisms (12 099
    steps, 24 removals and 24 additions, p V^gamma 3.4e-5 against 2e-2, mass drift 7.0e-13 against 1e-12), ADR 0213's
    piston channel on the piso path with 7 removals (continuity 3.3e-15, volume 8.9e-16) and with 7 additions; rcfd run
    gives the reports of the in-process run and rcfd validate locates the errors of both tables; located errors N1 to N6
    and ADR 0191's E1 to E4 and E6 to E13 hold; five mutations each failed their tests. Open: the mesh-speed step as the
    default (ADR 0207 Q2 (b), changes the bits of moving compressible runs: the maintainer's call), layer thresholds as
    keys (ADR 0191 Q1), box_3d sections in the Studio's lists (F-293). STATUS kept PARTIAL by the lead: the maintainer
    decided on 2026-11-06 that F-259 is not closed yet; with ADR 0257 every registered check of the remainder is met,
    and closing it stays the maintainer's. Follow-up: F-365.
- [~] **F-260** Parametric studies: CMA-ES and a real-fan study
  - depends on: F-249, F-126
  - acceptance: CMA-ES reaches the registered target on a multimodal analytic test function from a start where Nelder-Mead does not (limits registered in an ADR); a multi-objective study on the FAN-01 passage over at least two blade parameters, using a converged solver, returns a Pareto set whose members are re-run to confirm their reported objectives within 1 percent
  - note: Split from F-249 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Acceptance text proposed by the lead; refine when scheduled.
    Blocked on FAN-01 solver convergence (waves 43B-C). Size L.
    - PARTIAL (ADR 0222, the registration of F-260, 2026-11-08, branch f260-cmaes, not merged): the CMA-ES clause is
      met; the real-fan study is not attempted.
      - Built: the opt-in method `cma_es` (library `design::cmaes`, `Method::CmaEs`, the design tools' `{"type":
        "cma_es", budget, pop, sigma0, restarts, seed}`): the (mu/mu_W, lambda)-CMA-ES of Hansen's tutorial
        (arXiv:1604.00772v2, Fig. 6, Table 1 and Appendix B read; its source-code appendix not opened), with its
        termination criteria, the tutorial's box rule (62) (a sample outside the box is not evaluated and ranks last)
        and restarts with the population doubled (Auger and Hansen 2005).
      - Met: on the shifted Rastrigin function in 4 dimensions, from a start three local minima from the optimum in
        every coordinate, CMA-ES with 9 restarts reaches f <= 1e-8 within 40 000 evaluations on 20 of 20 seeds (limit 18
        of 20), while Nelder-Mead from the same start (default and ADR 0209 options, 40 runs) stops in the local minimum
        f = 35.82; the sphere and the ellipsoid of condition 1e6 in 10 dimensions reach 1e-10 on 20 of 20 seeds; the
        parameters, update, eigensolver, normal draws and termination criteria against their closed forms; study,
        propose / record, resume and tool checks; every mutation fails its test. Recorded: 3 of 20 seeds without
        restarts; 14 of 20 in 10 dimensions within 100 000 evaluations (Nelder-Mead 0 of 20).
      - Not attempted (ADR 0222 reading 2): the multi-objective FAN-01 study. FAN-01 has no converged solve (the
        second-order limit cycle of ADRs 0110 to 0181; the first-order example case of ADR 0176 ends not_converged at
        its cap), F-126 is partial, and no case key carries a scalar blade parameter (the blade is sixteen station
        lists). Defaults bit-identical. Open: ADR 0222 Q1 to Q5 (Q1: split the real-fan study into a new item and call
        F-260 done, recommended; Q2 the box rule; Q3 the defaults; Q4 the tool description; Q5 the restart points).

## Revision additions (F-261 to F-269)

Added after the static feature-gap review; wording is product-independent. Phases follow the phase headings above.

- [~] **F-261** Studio project folder library (rcfd-project)
  - depends on: F-145
  - acceptance: A project is a folder with a versioned manifest, case and mesh references and immutable run records; writes are atomic, a torn file is detected, old schema versions migrate, and a file watcher reports external edits. Limits are registered in ADR 0122 and checked by headless tests.
  - note: Wave 47A (ADR 0122) and audit fixes in ADR 0128. Library only, no window. Size M.
    - Not done: moving the run service onto these types (the runner keeps its own copies, to be unified), and the other
      additive contract items listed in the ADR addendum.
- [~] **F-262** Studio run service (rcfd-runner)
  - depends on: F-261
  - acceptance: A detached runner owns a queue of runs under a CPU and memory budget with pause, resume, cancel and crash recovery, and reports state through append-only status files. Kill tests show a killed runner leaves no run in a false running state. Limits are registered in ADR 0123.
  - note: Wave 47B (ADR 0123). Size L. One registered check (S5) is an ignored known miss.
    - Fixes in ADR 0128: no caller-chosen binary, status-write failure stops the run, liveness needs two misses, bounded
      output drain, argv quoting, no console window.
    - Memory probing uses typeperf with a time limit and a 5 s PowerShell fallback.
    - Not done: socket control (files only), runs started from the application.
- [~] **F-263** Studio time-series field store (rcfd-tsstore)
  - depends on: F-261
  - acceptance: The mesh is stored once and field snapshots per saved time are chunked, compressed and indexed, so a reader can jump to any saved time and read it back bit-exactly. A bad tail left by a crash is tolerated. Limits are registered in ADR 0124.
  - note: Wave 47C (ADR 0124). Library level. Size M.
    - Not done: residual and monitor series are not in the store yet, and the solver does not write to it.
- [~] **F-264** Studio wgpu render core v0 (rcfd-render)
  - depends on: F-263
  - acceptance: An offscreen wgpu renderer draws a surface mesh with per-vertex and per-cell scalars, colour maps and a camera, writes PNG, and is compared with a CPU reference by pixel statistics. Limits are registered in ADR 0125.
  - note: Wave 47D (ADR 0125), wgpu 30.0.1. Size L. Registered check P2 (picking returns the scalar value) is an ignored
    known miss.
    - Open decision: the egui front end (eframe 0.36.2) needs Rust 1.95 while the workspace builds on an older
      toolchain.
    - Not done: cut planes, iso-surfaces, streamlines, particles, video.
- [~] **F-265** Claude Code bridge library (rcfd-claude)
  - depends on: F-261
  - acceptance: The library lists Claude Code sessions for a project folder, tails a transcript, and sends a message to a closed session by resuming it in headless mode, with a conservative tool allow-list and no auto-approval. Behaviour was observed on one CLI build (2.1.310); a fixture set pins it.
  - note: Wave 47E (ADR 0126), fixes in ADR 0128 (allow-list refuses control files, fail-closed init check). Fixtures
    carry synthetic ids. Size M.
    - Not done: a sidecar for approvals (only if the allow-list proves too narrow), tests against other CLI versions.
- [ ] **F-266** Studio application shell (egui on wgpu)
  - depends on: F-262, F-263, F-264, F-265
  - acceptance: A window opens a project folder and shows its cases and runs with state, scrubs a run through time with linked fields and residuals, edits case inputs with schema validation, and hosts the Claude Code chat sidebar. The checks listed in docs/ui-restart-plan.md section 6 each exist as a named test. A person views the result and reports.
  - note: Wave 48 in docs/ui-restart-plan.md. Starts only after the wave 47 results have been viewed. Size XL.
- [ ] **F-267** Claude Code plugin with project tools
  - depends on: F-262, F-265
  - acceptance: A Claude Code plugin ships an MCP server (extending rcfd-mcp) with tools to list projects and runs, edit project files with validation, start and stop runs, read metrics and compare runs; edits made from Claude Code show in the application. Protocol tests pass and one real session is checked where possible.
  - note: Wave 48 in docs/ui-restart-plan.md. Size L.
- [~] **F-268** Design ledger and tolerance study driver
  - depends on: F-249
  - acceptance: Every design variant is recorded in a ledger with its inputs, solver version and results, and a
    tolerance study driver samples manufacturing spread and reports output spread against registered limits (ADR 0121).
  - note: Wave 46D (ADR 0121); Sobol indices ADR 0240 (merged 2026-11-12). Size M. Every model is a stated proxy until
    checked against measured fan data, which does not exist yet. BUILT (ADR 0240): the opt-in library function
    design::sensitivity::run gives first-order and total Sobol indices of independent inputs (the uq distributions) with
    delta-method standard errors, on the A, B, A_B^(i) Monte Carlo design (Saltelli 2002) at N (d + 2) evaluations, with
    the centred Saltelli et al. (2010) first-order and the Jansen (1999) total estimators; rows with a failed evaluation
    are dropped and counted; every evaluation and a sobol_summary can go to the ledger; bit-identical for any worker
    count. Met: Ishigami (N 16384) and a linear function with mixed distributions within 4 SE of the closed forms
    (largest z 2.41), a dummy input exactly zero, delta-method coverage 0.920 to 0.963 at 1.96 SE (400 runs, limit
    0.90), the interaction ST3 - S3 = 0.239 seen where SRC gives SRC_2^2 = 5e-6; six mutations caught (one after a
    corrected check). Known miss: the NC1 control on ST1 (|z| 3.87 against the a = 6 value, limit 4; the estimator meets
    its own limit). Not done: uncertainty bands on the reduced-order model, automatic ledger logging from runs, an MCP
    tool for uq or Sobol studies (changes the tools-list goldens). Open: ADR 0240 Q2, Q4, Q5. Follow-up for the tool
    exposure (ADR 0240 Q2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-339.
- [~] **F-269** Test gate speed and strictness
  - depends on: F-106
  - acceptance: The full gate runs each test in its own process from a small pool with a per-test time limit, prints the
    summary format the older scripts read, and a scanner lists tests that cannot fail (ADRs 0127 to 0129,
    docs/test-process.md).
  - note: Size M. Open items: an environment switch that makes the 12 data-gated tests fail rather than skip; limit
    headroom on one stage; a test for the R3 limit; a re-measurement at 5 jobs; scanning of inline test modules; a slot
    queue in place of the directory locks. The T2 vacuous pass is closed by ADR 0235 C: t2b asserts the registered
    precondition over(BDF2) >= 0.02 (measured 2.467e-2, bounded 1.16e-9); the old T2 stays as an ignored setup_defect
    record.

## Revision additions (F-270 to F-275)

Added with [ADR 0173](adr/0173-workspace-layer-between-the-project-folder-the-mcp-server-and-the-studio.md), one
workspace layer between the project folder, the MCP server and the Studio. Priority set by the maintainer on
2026-11-04: these items come before the FAN-01 diagnosis.

- [~] **F-270** Workspace layer (rcfd-workspace) shared by the MCP server and the Studio
  - depends on: F-261, F-262, F-267
  - acceptance: One crate holds the commands, queries and write rule for a project folder, and both the MCP project tools and the Studio use it: the existing project-tool and Studio tests pass unchanged, a Studio save and an edit_case on the same file give one write and one conflict naming the current hash, a comment line in a case survives a Studio save, and the crate graph stays acyclic with rcfd-studio not depending on rcfd-mcp (ADR 0173 W1, W2 and W5, checks C1, C2 and C6).
  - note: ADR 0173 (proposed 2026-11-04). Priority 1, set by the maintainer on 2026-11-04. Closes the race between
    Studio saves (save_if_base: no edit lock, no edits.jsonl entry) and edit_case. Size L.
    - PARTIAL (ADR 0185, the registration of F-270, 2026-11-05, branch f270-workspace, not merged): the crate exists and
      the MCP project tools run on it (W1, W2); the Studio saves under the edit lock with a journal line, creates cases
      and starts runs through it (W5).
    - Open: a comment line survives a Studio save only in the workspace's line-level form, which the Studio does not
      use, because the preview's save rule (ADR 0147, ADR 0148) and three Studio tests need the saved bytes to be the
      editor's whole text (ADR 0185 Q1, a maintainer question).
- [~] **F-271** New simulations from the MCP server in project mode
  - depends on: F-270
  - acceptance: In project mode the MCP server creates a case in cases/ (from a shipped example, a built-in template, TOML, settings or a copy of a project case, never replacing a file) and starts a run of it through the runner, in one call if asked, with the same start plan as the Studio, so the run's fields are stored and the Studio lists the run and can read its snapshots (ADR 0173 R1, W3, check C7, decisions D7 and D2).
  - note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 2. The shared start plan changes start_run's output for cases with no store
    setting, so it needs the maintainer's approval (D7). Size M.
    - PARTIAL (ADR 0186, the registration of F-271, 2026-11-05, branch f271-new-simulations, not merged): the project
      tool new_case makes cases/<name>.toml (or .json) from a shipped example, the built-in template, TOML, settings or
      a copy, validated first and never replacing a file; start_run makes a new case and runs it in one call with the
      Studio's field-store plan, so its fields are stored, and the Studio's run poller and store reader show it (C7).
    - Open:
      - start_run of an existing case applies the plan only with store: "plan", because the default change waits for
        the maintainer's approval of D7 (ADR 0186 Q2);
      - the project tool is named new_case because the session tool create_case is the only way to make a session, so
        D2's hiding is left to F-275 (ADR 0186 Q1);
      - the Studio still uses its own copy of the start plan, pinned equal by a parity test, until the maintainer's
        Studio work lands.
- [~] **F-272** Mesh set-up from the MCP server in project mode
  - depends on: F-270
  - acceptance: In project mode the MCP server checks a case's mesh (the report of rcfd check-mesh and the patch list), draws it with the CPU renderer, imports a Gmsh, Fluent or OpenFOAM file from the project folder into meshes/ with its cell, face and patch counts, lists meshes/ with the cases that use each file, and returns the mesh check when edit_case changes a mesh setting; an invalid mesh setting is refused with a located diagnostic and writes nothing (ADR 0173 R2, W4, check C8, decision D8).
  - note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 3. Not included: a mesh recipe format and the surface-to-volume pipeline, which no case or command reaches today (D8 (b), a later ADR). Size M. PARTIAL (ADR 0187, the registration of F-272, 2026-11-05, branch f272-mesh-setup, not merged): the project tools check_case_mesh (the report of rcfd check-mesh and the patch list of a case's mesh), preview_mesh (a PNG coloured by a cell-quality measure, drawn by the CPU renderer), import_mesh (a Gmsh or Fluent file or an OpenFOAM folder read with the solver's readers, its cells, faces, patches, zones and bounds reported, copied into meshes/ without replacing anything) and list_meshes (meshes/ with the cases that use each mesh); edit_case builds and checks the edited mesh when a mesh setting changes and refuses, writing nothing, a mesh file outside the project (1004) or a mesh that cannot be built (1003, located); a case's mesh file is confined to the project folder by every mesh command (C8). Open: the check is named check_case_mesh because the session tool check_mesh holds the name until F-275 (ADR 0187 Q1); a mesh that builds but fails the quality check is written with mesh.ok false (Q2); no size limit on a mesh build (Q3); a preview over the size budget is drawn narrower (Q4); non-orthogonality is the default measure (Q5); the three new read tools are not in the Studio bridge's allow-list (Q6, the maintainer's); the public Fluent elbow is checked only where it is fetched.
    - USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0187 decision record): the Studio's size limits, through a preview::estimate shared
      in the workspace, follow once the maintainer's Studio worktree has landed (Q3 (b), F-293); Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5 and Q6
      were not asked (Q6 is (b) on main since F-275).
- [~] **F-273** Project journal and change feed with who, what and why; the Studio updates from it
  - depends on: F-270
  - acceptance: Every accepted write, case creation, mesh import, run submission and run control call appends an entry to .rcfd/edits.jsonl with an actor, a sequence number, the settings changed (path, old and new value) and an optional reason (additive fields only); one ordered feed merges the journal, the run records and events, and the watcher's changes; a change made by one process appears in a second process's feed within the limit fixed by an amendment of ADR 0173, a write made outside the workspace appears as external, and the Studio updates its views from the feed and shows who changed what and why (ADR 0173 R3, W6, check C3, decision D4).
  - note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 4. Linking an MCP actor to a Claude Code session is NOT VERIFIED (ADR 0173 D4).
    Size M.
    - PARTIAL (ADR 0188, the registration of F-273, 2026-11-05, branch f273-journal-feed, not merged): every accepted write, case creation, mesh import, run submission and accepted run request of the workspace, from the MCP server and from the Studio, leaves one line in .rcfd/edits.jsonl with seq (given under a short project-wide lock), who, the actor {client, instance {pid, started}} (mcp, or studio for the Studio's saves and creations), the reason the caller gave and the changed settings with old and new values (additive fields and kinds only; lines written before still read); the feed (rcfd_workspace::feed, the MCP tool read_feed) merges the journal, the runs' state, warning and stop events and the watcher's changes, and labels a change no journal line explains external with its path only; an edit_case with a reason made by the rcfd-mcp binary reaches another process's feed at the first poll of 250 ms (limit 4), a plain write within 4 polls; the Studio's project worker reads the feed and says who changed what and why for changes another actor made (C3).
    - Open: the Studio's run starts and controls are journaled without an actor until the maintainer's Studio worktree lands (ADR 0188 Q3); the run worker, a feed panel and a notes list in the Studio wait for that worktree (Q5); the feed is offered as the new tool read_feed, list_changes unchanged (Q1); a write_note line keeps kind edit (Q2); linking an mcp actor to a Claude Code session is NOT VERIFIED and not built (Q4); read_feed is not in the Studio bridge's allow-list (Q6, the maintainer's); a feed shows no history from before it was opened (Q7).
    - USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0188 decision record): the Studio's actor on its run starts and controls (Q3 (a))
      and a feed panel and notes list (Q5 (a)) follow once the maintainer's Studio worktree has landed (F-293); no link
      from an mcp actor to a Claude Code session for now (Q4 (c)); Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7 and the run worker of Q5 were not
      asked.
- [~] **F-274** Design study evaluations as runner runs in project mode
  - depends on: F-270, F-268
  - acceptance: In project mode each design evaluation is submitted to the runner as a run tagged with its study and variant (additive run-record fields), never more than max_runs at once; the metrics match the in-process evaluator for the same cases within the tolerance fixed by an amendment of ADR 0173, and the extra cost per evaluation is measured and recorded (ADR 0173 W7, check C4).
  - note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 5. Chained studies need the runner to start a run from a previous result; runner
    support for continue_from is not established. Size M.
    - PARTIAL (ADR 0189, the registration of F-274, 2026-11-05, branch f274-design-evals, not merged): with --project, design_run_study and design_evaluate evaluate each candidate at each operating condition as one run of the project's runner, the base case with rcfd run --set entries checked to give the in-process settings tree, tagged in run.json with study, variant and condition (three optional fields, absent from every other run); the result is read from metrics.json by the in-process status rule; three points on the 32 x 32 cavity gave three tagged runs, at most max_runs = 2 at once, with records equal to the in-process ones bit for bit; one evaluation cost 0.64 s on the runner against 0.23 s in process (C4).
    - Open: a chained study with several conditions, a study with its own max_steps and operating maps stay in the server process (the runner cannot start a run from another run's result or cap its steps; ADR 0189 Q2, Q3); runs that outlive a call are submitted again (Q5); no journal line for design runs and records yet (Q6, now that F-273 is merged); the design tools keep the access class write_files though they now start runs (Q7, F-275); the run-record fields need the lead's approval (Q4, ADR 0130).
    - USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0189 decision record): the run-record fields study, variant and condition are
      approved flat as built (Q4 (a), the lead's approval under ADR 0130); a runner setting to continue from a previous
      run, with a step cap, is the new item F-287 (Q2 (d), Q3 (d)); adopting matching runs is the new item F-288 (Q5
      (b)); design_run_study and design_evaluate become access class execute, made separately (Q7); Q1, Q6 and Q8 were
      not asked.
- [~] **F-275** Project-mode MCP tool list and plugin edit hook
  - depends on: F-271, F-272, F-274
  - acceptance: With --project, each session tool is hidden once its project equivalent has passed its check, until tools/list holds no tool whose state lives only in the server's memory; without --project it is byte-identical to before; the plugin refuses Claude Code's own Edit and Write under cases/, runs/ and designs/ with a message naming edit_case and create_case, checked in a real session where possible (ADR 0173 W8, check C5, decisions D2 and D5).
  - note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 6. The hook contract is to be checked on an installed Claude Code build first.

    - PARTIAL (ADR 0195, the registration of F-275, 2026-11-06, branch f275-project-mode-tools, not merged): with --project

## Revision additions (F-284 to F-293)

Added with the maintainer's answers of 2026-11-06 to the open questions of ADR 0183 and ADRs 0187 to 0195; each of those
ADRs ends with a decision record of 2026-11-06. F-276 to F-283 are held by the milestone roadmap on the unmerged branch
m0-gate-roadmap, which ADRs 0183 and 0184 already cite, so these items start at F-284. Every limit of these items is
fixed by the item's registration ADR before any code.

- [ ] **F-284** Particle splash and rebound at a wall film (impact regime maps)
  - depends on: F-253
  - acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. Parcels that reach the wall film of F-253
    are absorbed, rebound or splash by an impact regime map taken from a published source that the ADR names and reads
    (constants read from the source): for parcel streams set in each regime the model gives the regime and the rebound
    or splash outcome of the source's relations, and the parcel mass ledger of F-253 (injected = airborne + deposited +
    escaped + stuck + film + drained) balances with the new outcomes counted, each within limits fixed by its
    registration ADR; runs without the new setting are unchanged bit for bit (the records R1 to R4 of ADRs 0192 and 0194
    and the baseline hashes unchanged).

    potential not wired; body_force_weighted refused with pressure options; other solvers and models refused; P1 binding

    - DONE (ADR 0221, 2026-11-07, branch f298-joule-heat, not merged). (a) With
      solver.gradient_equations.electric_potential the boundary current density and the Joule heat use the currents of
      the operator the potential was solved with (rcfd-fv electric::face_currents_opt, joule_heat_opt,
      boundary_power_opt; a cell's Joule heat is half the face power F_f (phi_o - phi_n) of its internal faces plus F_b
      (phi_P - phi_b) of its boundary faces, so the total is the boundary power up to the solver's residual). On the
      29.6-degree wedge, for the seven option sets, the boundary currents add up to zero within the solver tolerance (at
      most 2.2e-16 A against bounds of 2.2e-12 A), per group of cells too, and the Joule heat equals the electric power
      to 5e-16 W (P 0.24 to 0.27 W); the tree's current density and heat are the library's. The unchanged currents miss
      the domain balance by 4.7e-7 to 1.9e-3 A (every set that changes boundary faces) and a group balance for every
      set; the unchanged Joule heat misses the power by 3.0e-2 to 3.6e-2 W; the default's own Joule heat misses its
      power by 3.1e-2 W (11.9 percent) on the skewed mesh (kept, ADR 0221 Q1). (b) Measured first: in a converged SIMPLE
      channel on the wedge with a fixed-pressure outlet and one corrector the default flux correction leaves a domain
      mass imbalance of 2.0e-3 of the inflow and 6.8e-4 in one outlet cell (interior 3e-14; 5.0e-3 with SIMPLEC and its
      compensation; with gradient_boundary dropped 2e-13), which matters by the registered rule (1e-6). So under the
      pressure options (solver.gradient_equations.pressure) the flux correction now takes the equation's non-orthogonal
      part on fixed-pressure faces (owner, corrected or none): on the 38-degree box it carries the operator's flux to
      7.3e-16 of the cell scale on the outlet cells (6.6e-2 to 2.6e-1 without), and the converged channel runs close
      their mass balance (at most 1.3e-12 of the inflow) for six sets. Defaults bit-identical (the default and dropped
      runs' hashes, the settings hash and every field of the electric case unchanged; baseline hashes and H1 unedited).
      Amendment 2: Some(GradientOptions::default()) is None in the new functions (found by ADR 0204 G4 (iv)). Open: the
      default Joule heat on skewed meshes (Q1), the default flux correction on fixed-pressure faces (Q2), a negative
      cell Joule heat under the options (Q3, none seen), the SIMPLEC boundary compensation under the options (Q4).

- [x] **F-302** Periodic seam pair diffusivity: remaining viscosities and the pimple check
  - depends on: F-296, F-294
  - acceptance: Pair diffusivity covers the temperature-dependent properties viscosity and the user-function viscosity;
    a case-tree check of k-epsilon and Spalart-Allmaras with pair on pimple.
  - note: From ADR 0212 questions 1 and 4, recommendations taken by the lead. RSM on a rotational seam only if RSM ever
    runs there.
    - BUILT (ADR 0227, the registration of F-302, 2026-11-08, branch f302-pair-diffusivity, not merged): every
      registered check is met. turbulence.periodic_seam.diffusivity = "pair" is now accepted on a laminar run with a
      temperature-dependent properties.viscosity law or a user-function viscosity (R1''): both faces of a pair take mu(w
      T_P + (1 - w) T_Q) / rho, or the module's value at the centre of the pair's face of lower index with the
      temperature and speed interpolated across the seam (one call per pair). Finding: the property viscosity is already
      one value per pair by default, up to rounding (0 to 5.6e-16), so pair changes its last bits on graded seams only.
      The user-function budgets close to 4.5e-16 with pair and miss by 1.2e-4 to 1.3e-3 with owner. On pimple, k-epsilon
      and SA with pair give one momentum face viscosity per pair to the bit (owner 5.2e-3 to 1.6e-2), the laminar rule
      holds across the seam, and the transient k and nuTilda sweep budgets close to 3.1e-15 (owner 1.4e-4 to 3.5e-2).
      The cases of the ignored F-294 S1 run again in ADR 0227 S1t. Defaults bit-identical. Open: ADR 0227 Q1 to Q5 (the
      position of a user function on a pair, the energy diffusivity on a seam, pair for the property law, the F-294
      record, one call per pair).

  - depends on: F-219

    bit-identical, state hashes checked): the flux of every fluid-solid face is that of the linear extension of the
    fluid profile through the no-slip value at the surface crossing, the net flux of each body is that of its rigid
    velocity, and the solid cells get the volume source that releases their continuity (`reconstruct_face_flux`; one
    statement and the source of the plain pressure solve in SimpleSolver and PimpleSolver). Measured (limits registered
    before the code): circular Couette, the F-219 V1 check, error 6.12e-3, 1.61e-3, 4.24e-4 at N 24, 48, 96, observed
    order 1.925 (limit 1.5; 2.04 from 96 to 192) against 1.023 of the forcing of ADR 0218, error at N 96 3.7 times
    smaller; face-flux error 39 times smaller; PISO equal to SIMPLEC to 1e-4; DFG 2D-1 on M2 C_D -0.31 %, C_L +2.53 %;
    eight mutations caught. Cause of the first order of ADR 0218 (derived and seen in the numbers): the continuity of a
    solid cell pins the flux of its fluid-solid face to the rigid velocity, a face velocity error of order h with a
    pressure jump of order 1. Not included: a case key or Studio control (schema golden); not the default; plain
    pressure path only (gradient options, body-force-weighted and implicit non-orthogonal pressure panic); the force and
    moment from the forcing stay first order (CC torque error 1.60 %, 0.74 %, 0.39 % at N 48, 96, 192); the continuity
    measure holds the solid-cell sources; the limits of F-219 (no moving bodies, momentum only, not in the coupled
    solver, the fractional step or on moving meshes). Follow-ups (ADR 0234 questions 2 to 6, recommendations taken on
    the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-337 (second-order force and moment); the case key, the guard
    refusals, the continuity measure and the corrector trial solve go with F-307. Open: question 1 (the second-order
    forcing as the default changes existing numbers). FOUND LATER (ADR 0249, 2026-11-12): the second-order forcing
    stopped at step 6 of DFG 2D-2 on M2 in PISO with BDF2 (divergence guard, Courant 1.1e7); it had been run in PISO
    only on circular Couette flow. DIAGNOSED (ADR 0254, 2026-11-12, F-355): the linear extension of D1 has a weight of
    up to 38 where the surface crossing lies close to the fluid cell centre, and at an impulsive start, or with a time
    step small against h^2/nu (circular Couette with dt 2.5e-5 grows to 281), what it multiplies is not small;
    `build_second_order` is unchanged and is refused by PimpleSolver with a located message in that range; transient
    runs use `build_second_order_bounded` (ADR 0254), which keeps the order (1.947 on circular Couette). Open: whether
    `build_second_order` should build the bounded form (ADR 0254 question 1).

- [~] **F-331** Sponge layer for the compressible solver
  - depends on: F-243
  - acceptance: A plane pulse leaving through a sponge layer at 0, 30, 45 and 60 degrees reflects less than 1 percent; a
    case without a sponge is bit-identical.
  - note: From ADR 0233 question 4. The job of 2026-11-12 (ADR 0237). The acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY, not
    from a case file. Built: an opt-in sponge layer of the compressible solver (rcfd-fv sponge.rs,
    `CompressibleSolver::set_sponge`), in two forms: `Plain` (every conserved variable relaxes to a reference state) and
    `Matched` (a perfectly matched layer of linear acoustics about a state at rest: mass, energy and normal momentum
    relax, the tangential momentum is forced through one scalar of memory per cell); polynomial profile, peak rate from
    the wanted two-way attenuation (`rate_max_for_reflection`). The registration showed beforehand that the plain form
    cannot reach 1 percent at 45 and 60 degrees in a practical thickness (175 pulse widths at 60 degrees), so the
    acceptance is met by the matched form. Measured (limit 1 percent, layer of 40 cells, largest difference to a run on
    an extended grid against the incident peak): normal incidence 9.2e-7 in front of the Thompson boundary and 1.1e-6 in
    front of a rigid wall; one isolated plane pulse 2.4e-5 at 30 degrees and 1.4e-4 at 45 degrees; pulse trains in a
    rigid duct 1.2e-4, 2.8e-4, 1.2e-3 at 30, 45, 60 degrees (the Thompson boundary alone 0.081, 0.196, 0.372; the plain
    form at 45 degrees 0.150). Without a sponge the solver is bit-identical (the F-258 bit records and the ADR 0233
    tests pass unedited; a set-and-cleared sponge and a zero-rate sponge give the same bits). Six mutations caught. One
    amendment: the first oblique set-up (a wave train started inside the layer with zero memory) measured 3.8e-2,
    6.2e-2, 8.7e-2 and was diagnosed as a defective set-up before the corrected runs; its tests are kept as ignored
    records. Not done: case-schema wiring (a new key needs an approved edit of a registered hash test; this is why the
    status is partial). Limits: the matched form is one planar layer with a reference at rest, does not damp waves along
    the layer (a transient inside the layer leaves transverse standing waves in a rigid duct, the 4 to 9 percent of the
    first set-up) and has a memory without decay; the plain form is quiet only near normal incidence; 60 degrees is
    checked with pulse trains, not with an isolated pulse; explicit source (`rate dt` well below 2.5, `max_dt` does not
    know it); not on moving meshes; Cartesian grids, gas at rest. Open questions in ADR 0237 addendum 1 (wiring, an
    isolated pulse at 60 degrees, memory decay and damping along the layer, `max_dt`, moving meshes). Follow-ups
    (recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): the wiring goes with F-330; F-340
    (memory decay, damping along the layer, corners); F-341 (moving meshes).
- [~] **F-332** Frequency-dependent wall impedance (time-domain model)
  - depends on: F-243
  - acceptance: The reflection coefficient of a mass-spring-damper wall matches the closed form in magnitude and phase

  - note: From ADR 0233, proposed follow-up, taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. The job of
    2026-11-12 (ADR 0243): the acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY, not from a case file. Built: `MsdWall { p, r, m, k
    }` (rcfd-fv compressible_bc.rs; `CompressibleSolver::set_msd_wall`, `msd_wall_state`, `set_msd_wall_state`,
    `msd_dt_limit`), a locally reacting mass-spring-damper wall with the impedance Z(omega) = r + i(omega m - k/omega):
    displacement and velocity per face, advanced with the solver's Runge-Kutta stages; the face keeps the outgoing
    Riemann invariant of ADR 0233 and takes the wall velocity; m = 0 is the algebraic form and m = k = 0 is
    `CompBc::Impedance` bit for bit; the wall's step limit 0.8 min(2m/(r + rho c), (r + rho c)/k) is part of `max_dt`
    and a larger step is refused. Registered checks, all met at the first run, no amendment: a tone at 0.8, 1 and 1.25
    times the resonance frequency, complex reflection coefficient by a least-squares split into incident and reflected
    wave at 400 probes: magnitude within 2.9e-4 (limit 2e-2), phase within 2.4e-4 rad (limit 1.93e-2 rad, the strictest
    reading of 2 percent) of (Z - rho c)/(Z + rho c) = 0.797 at -55.3 degrees, 1/3 at 180 degrees, 0.797 at +55.3
    degrees; the same measurement on walls with a known real reflection (impedance rho c/2 and rigid) within 1.3e-4 and
    5e-5 rad; a wall without damper reflects with magnitude 1 within 2.8e-3; free decay of the wall with the radiation
    damping rho c within 1.2e-6; a light mass and a stiff spring at a third and a sixth of the CFL step stable and
    within 4.3e-5 of their limits; 1400 steps bit-identical with the impedance wall at m = k = 0; a cleared wall and the
    existing compressible tests (F-258 bit records, ADR 0233, ADR 0237) bit-identical and unedited. Eight mutations
    caught. Not done: case-schema wiring (a new key needs an approved edit of case_hashes_w48u.rs; this is why the
    status is partial). Limits: one degree of freedom per face, no coupling between faces, no multi-pole fit of a
    measured impedance; the mesh face does not move (transpiration velocity; mass crosses the face and returns); normal
    incidence only checked; not together with a sponge, not on moving meshes; gas at rest, Cartesian grids, verification
    against closed forms only. The wiring (with one oblique angle and the wall together with a sponge, ADR 0243
    questions 1 to 3, recommendations taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11) goes with F-330.

  - depends on: F-314
  - acceptance: Set-up RL of ADR 0232 (component at rest, fringe phase locked) on levels 1 to 4: the root mean square of
    the error of the calculated component cells converges at order 1.7 or more between successive levels, or the ADR
    names the source of the first-order term (coefficient 1.0e-4) with a number.
  - note: From ADR 0232 question 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR
    0246 (registration of F-334, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): PARTIAL, a diagnosis, tests only, no library change.
    The order check is missed: RL on levels 1 to 4 gives 1.549e-4, 6.39e-5, 3.98e-5, 2.49e-5 in the root mean square of
    the calculated component cells, orders 1.277, 1.166, 1.626 (limit 1.7); the fit of ADR 0232 predicted 2.86e-5 at
    level 4. The source is named: the truncation of the linear donor interpolation. With stencils exact for biquadratic
    fields on both fringes (nine cells, test code) the error is 3.24e-4, 8.55e-5, 3.90e-5, 2.23e-5, orders 1.922, 1.935,
    1.950, and equals the error of the background alone. The error with the library stencils is the sum of that part and
    of the response to the truncation, which is 1.35 to 1.90 times larger, opposed to it (cosine -0.96 to -0.88) and
    converges at 1.693, 1.588, 1.800; they cancel to 88 to 96 percent, so the library stencils give the smaller error at
    levels 1 and 2 and the lower order. The coefficient 1.0e-4 is the increment per level of that response times L^2
    (1.04e-4, 0.98e-4, then 0.38e-4). Its part from the background fringe is of first order on levels 1 to 3 (4.9e-5,
    2.2e-5, 1.41e-5: 1.153, 1.093) and still growing at t = 0.5; the part from the component fringe converges at 1.782,
    1.698. Ruled out with numbers: a time error, the single-mesh solution, the outer boundary of the component, the
    reference cell, the interpolated pressure and the convection (the error is linear in the amplitude to 0.07 percent),
    a mass defect, the flux at the fringe faces, the transient Rhie-Chow term; with coincident meshes the coupling gives
    the background alone to 7e-9. Traced by ADR 0340 (F-349): the normal velocity of a fringe cell is imposed on the
    calculated cells through a resistance proportional to nu / h (a flux defect held by a pressure jump dJ = -(16 nu / 3
    h) D), so the response per unit of truncation grows with the refinement; the truncation of the background fringe of
    RL also alternates between odd and even levels. Controls held, four mutations caught. Follow-ups (ADR 0246 questions
    2 and 4, recommendations taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-336 with RL added to its
    acceptance, and F-349 on the response to the background fringe.

    calculated and fringe cells of TG_L converges at order 1.7 or more on levels 1 to 3 with dt proportional to h^2, the
    root mean square of the error of the calculated component cells of RL of ADR 0232 converges at order 1.7 or more on
    levels 1 to 4 (ADR 0246 TQ: 1.922, 1.935, 1.950 with test-supplied stencils), the uniform-flow check U1 of ADR 0219
    holds, and the default stencils and results are bit-identical.
  - note: From ADR 0232 question 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR
    0251 (registration of F-336, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): DONE pending acceptance. Built: an opt-in of
    rcfd_mesh::overset, Overset::set_donor_interpolation(DonorInterpolation::Quadratic): the stencil of a fringe cell is
    the donor and the calculated cells that share a point with it (9 on quadrilaterals, 27 on hexahedra; a fringe or
    hole cell is never a donor), with the weights of the weighted least-squares quadratic (the minimum of sum w^2/omega
    under the reproduction of the 6 monomials in 2-D, 10 in 3-D, by a pivoted Householder QR). The weights sum to one,
    can be negative (smallest -0.067, sum of absolute values 1.40 on a whole block) and are not clipped; a stencil with
    fewer cells than monomials, of deficient rank or with a sum of absolute values above 4 keeps the linear stencil and
    is listed (Connectivity::fallbacks, OversetInfo::n_fallback), and a step whose interpolated rAU is not positive is
    refused. Met: quadratics are reproduced to 1e-15 on Cartesian, distorted, O-grid and sheared 3-D donor meshes; the
    truncation converges at 3.00; TG_L with dt proportional to h^2 converges at 1.993 and 2.000 on levels 1 to 3
    (largest error 7.68e-4, 1.93e-4, 8.58e-5, now in a background cell at the domain boundary; 1.0785e-3, 3.514e-4,
    1.712e-4 with the linear stencils); the calculated component cells of RL converge at 1.916, 1.924, 1.952 on levels 1
    to 4 (3.20e-4, 8.48e-5, 3.89e-5, 2.22e-5); the uniform flow holds to 1.1e-14; coincident meshes give the background
    alone to 6e-12; no fallback and no unconverged solve on the registered set-ups; without the opt-in the stencils are
    those of ADR 0219 bit for bit, Q0 and the records R2 hold. Said plainly: on the two coarsest levels of RL the
    calculated component cells have 2.07 and 1.33 times the error of the linear stencils (the cancellation of ADR 0246),
    0.98 and 0.89 at levels 3 and 4. Limits: a donor next to a wall or to its own fringe ring falls back to the linear
    stencil; no flow run of the cylinder case or in 3-D with the opt-in. Six mutations caught. Found on the way: the
    donor search of F-134 finds no donor in cells with non-planar faces. Open for the maintainer: whether the opt-in
    should become the default (ADR 0251 Q1). Follow-ups (ADR 0251 questions 2 and 5, recommendation taken on the
    maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-352, F-353. Open: question 1 (the quadratic interpolation as the
    default changes a default). no flow run in 3-D with the opt-in; the cylinder case TR with it is F-353 (ADR 0259:
    acceptance met, no fallback, mean drag error 3.42e-3 against 3.21e-3 of the linear stencils, recommendation against
    the default)
- [x] **F-337** Immersed solid: second-order force and moment
  - depends on: F-309
  - acceptance: The torque on the immersed rotating cylinder of circular Couette flow (the CC set-up of ADR 0218,
    second-order forcing) reaches an observed order of 1.5 between N 48 and 96, and the DFG 2D-1 drag and lift on M2 are
    within 1 percent and 3 percent of the FeatFlow values.
  - note: DONE in the library (ADR 0239, 2026-11-12), pending acceptance. From ADR 0234 question 5. Diagnosis by
    measurement (five hypotheses registered before any code): the force of the forcing was never first order (it is the
    momentum balance of the forced cells, its error that of the velocity field); the moment was, because `force_moment`
    applies the modification term of a first fluid cell at the surface crossing and not at the centre of its cell (1.49
    and 0.72 percent of the torque at N 48 and 96); the one-sided wall difference, the staircase face pressure, the
    quadrature at the crossings (order 1.50) and the momentum of the mass-source cells were measured and ruled out.
    Delivered: rcfd-fv immersed.rs, `ImmersedForcing::force_moment_second_order` (opt-in; `force_moment` unchanged and
    bit-identical, hashes checked): the same force, and the moment with every term at the centre of its cell, which is
    the angular-momentum balance of the forced cells, that is the moment of the full traction and momentum flux on the
    regular fluid faces around them (derived in the ADR; checked against that sum to 1.5e-6 of the torque). Measured
    (limits registered before the code): circular Couette torque error 0.396, 0.107, 0.027, 0.0069 percent at N 24, 48,
    96, 192, observed order 1.98 between 48 and 96 (limit 1.5; 1.96 from 96 to 192) against 1.11 of `force_moment`; DFG
    2D-1 on M2 C_D -0.306 %, C_L +2.534 % (limits 1 % and 3 %; the force is that of `force_moment`, unchanged); six
    mutations caught. Not included: the new evaluation as the default of `force_moment` (open, a change of a default);
    unsteady flow (the momentum of the forced cells); any caller outside the tests, a case key; non-orthogonal meshes;
    the limits of F-219 and F-309. Follow-up (ADR 0239 Q3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction
    of 2026-11-11): F-346. Open: Q1 (the cell arms as the moment of force_moment changes a default).

    Built: OversetSolver::set_time_scheme(Bdf2), an opt-in of the solver (OversetSolver::new still refuses BDF2, so no

    outer iteration extrapolated as the library does; only crates/rcfd-fv/src/overset.rs changed. Defaults bit for bit:

    cell calculated on a mesh at rest the step equals the library's BDF2 step bit for bit; the library has no BDF2 on a
    moving mesh, so the moving terms are checked by a uniform flow on a deforming mesh (3e-15) and through a moving,

    from 1.69e-4 to 2.1e-5 (limit 1.2e-4). Missed (acceptance): its ratio to max abs(d_400) is 2.46 (limit 4): located,
    not explained: the library's own BDF2 step on a single mesh at rest leaves 5.1e-6 with the ratio 2.30, independent
    of the start, the correctors and the outer iterations; the five times larger remainder on the coupled meshes is not

    motion of the component through the coupling). Missed (acceptance): T1c of ADR 0219 with BDF2 is 1.664 (limit 1.7):
    with BDF2 the error of both levels is free of time error (0.2 and 0.3 percent between 200 and 800 steps), so this is
    the spatial order of the pointwise maximum diagnosed by ADR 0232; the 1.80 observed in ADR 0238 was time error at
    level 1. Two set-up checks were defective and corrected by amendments; six mutations caught. Not delivered: the
    case-tree wiring. BDF2 for the library's moving-mesh step and the three-level follow conditions of a moving wall
    came with F-345 (ADR 0379; prepare takes them when BDF2 is on, and the BDF2 overset step with every cell calculated
    equals the library's bit for bit). Follow-ups (ADR 0241 questions 1, 4 and 5, recommendation taken on the

- [~] **F-340** Matched sponge layer: memory decay, damping along the layer, corners
  - depends on: F-331
  - acceptance: The set-up D record of ADR 0237 (a wave train started inside the layer with zero memory in a rigid duct)
    falls below 1 percent within its registered window; a constant pressure offset with a gradient along the layer gives
    a bounded tangential momentum over 100 transit times of the layer; a pulse leaving through the corner of two layers
    reflects less than 1 percent; an isolated plane pulse at 60 degrees reflects less than 1 percent; the checks A0,
    A30b, A45b, A60b, X1 and X45 of ADR 0237 still meet 1 percent.
  - note: From ADR 0237 questions 2 and 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11.
    The job of 2026-11-12 (ADR 0248): four of the five clauses are MET IN THE LIBRARY, clause 1 is MISSED with a
    diagnosis that the registration gave before the runs. Built (rcfd-fv sponge.rs, opt-in, `Plain` and `Matched`
    untouched): `SpongeForm::MatchedShifted(MatchedOptions { normal, shift, along, second })`, the matched layer as a
    complex coordinate stretching with (i) a complex frequency shift `shift` (the memories decay: under a held pressure
    the memory and the force along the layer saturate at p'/a instead of growing; below omega ~ a the layer does not
    absorb and it leaves a static offset alone), (ii) a second planar layer with an orthogonal normal for a corner
    (`Sponge::corner`: the same memory, one product term, the force of each layer on the momentum along the other's
    normal; a second memory for an edge in three dimensions), (iii) a damping of the momentum along the layer `along` (a
    mismatch with a measured price); `Sponge::planar_shifted`, `CompressibleSolver::sponge_memories` and
    `set_sponge_memories`. Measured with shift 0.25/s (0.05 c/L) and along 0 on the 40-cell layer of ADR 0237 (limit 1
    percent, largest difference to a run on an extended grid against the incident peak): an isolated plane pulse at 60
    degrees 8.1e-4 (the form of ADR 0237 in the same run 8.0e-4; 705 000 and 770 000 cells, the set-up of X45 with tails
    of 3.5 pulse widths and a reference grid shortened by a causality argument that a model confirmed to 12 digits); a
    quarter of a cylindrical pulse through two layers and their corner 5.3e-5 (no sponge 0.058, one layer 0.029); the
    checks of ADR 0237 repeated with the shift: A0 9.4e-7 (1.2e-6 in front of a rigid wall), A30b, A45b, A60b 3.1e-4,
    3.6e-4, 1.3e-3, X1 2.3e-5, X45 1.4e-4; a closed box with a pressure offset varying along the layer over 100 transit
    times: momentum along the layer at most 3.0 delta/c and not growing (the form of ADR 0237 in the same run 3.2 and
    not growing either: in a run neither form grows, the difference is under a held pressure, checked by algebra to
    4e-6). Without the options the new form produces the bits of `Matched`; the existing compressible, F-258, ADR 0233,
    ADR 0237 and ADR 0243 tests pass unedited. Eight mutations caught. MISSED, clause 1: the set-up D record (a wave
    train started inside the layer with zero memory in a rigid duct) stays at 3.7e-2, 6.1e-2, 8.6e-2 at 30, 45, 60
    degrees with the shift (3.8e-2, 6.2e-2, 8.7e-2 without) and at 2.2e-2, 3.6e-2, 4.2e-2 with along = 0.05, against
    1e-2; kept as three ignored known_miss records. Diagnosis (ADR 0248 DR12, a scratch model predicted the five numbers
    within 20 percent before the runs): the ringing sits at the cut-off frequencies of the duct; a field that does not
    vary across the layer solves the equations of every matched layer, so no matched layer damps it; a damping along the
    layer is a mismatch that reflects about 1.3 along of a pulse at 60 degrees whatever its frequency (along = 0.05
    measured 4.4e-2 of the steady train at 60 degrees), and the strength needed to remove the ringing within the
    registered window costs far more than 1 percent. Not a parameter that could be tuned at this thickness. Limits:
    linear acoustics about a state at rest; one layer or two orthogonal ones (no corner of three layers; the
    three-dimensional edge is checked by algebra only); explicit source; not on moving meshes; not with a
    mass-spring-damper wall; library only (the wiring goes with F-330); Cartesian grids. Open questions in ADR 0248
    addendum 1 (what to do with clause 1; a default for the shift in the wiring; whether to keep `along`; a corner run
    in three dimensions). Open: the default shift in the F-330 wiring (a default; ADR 0248 question 2). The clause-1
    follow-up (a plain damping zone behind a thicker layer) is proposed in ADR 0248 only for when a ducted case shows
    the ringing; no item added.
- [x] **F-341** Sponge layer on moving meshes
  - depends on: F-331, F-258
  - acceptance: With a sponge, a uniform reference state stays to round-off under `step_ale` on a deforming mesh; the
    ADR 0237 tube check on a uniformly translating mesh reflects less than 1 percent; without a sponge `step_ale` is
    bit-identical.
  - note: From ADR 0237 question 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR
    0265, 2026-11-12: the acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY. Built (rcfd-fv, opt-in): `sponge::SpongeFrame {
    StaticMesh (default: step_ale refuses a sponge, as before), AttachedToMesh }` and
    `CompressibleSolver::set_sponge_frame`. When attached, the rates (of both layers of a corner) and the memories
    belong to the cells and move with them; the reference stays a lab-frame state; the memory of a cell is the time
    integral of p - p_ref along its path; and `step_ale` adds the source at the volume of each Runge-Kutta stage, which
    keeps the damping consistent with the geometric conservation law (a uniform offset decays as exp(-rate t) for any
    deformation). `replace_mesh` still refuses a sponge, because the solver has no map from old to new cells and a
    matched layer reset under a wave rings: clear it, replace the mesh, then set a new sponge and the caller's mapped
    memories. Measured: a uniform reference state on the deforming set-up U of ADR 0207 stays within 3.3e-15 over 121 to
    136 steps in the plain, matched and shifted-corner forms (limit 1e-12); the ADR 0237 tube with both grids
    translating at Mach 0.2 reflects 9.6e-7 (plain and matched, Thompson end and pressure-release end) and 9.8e-7
    (shifted) against 1e-2; on a mesh whose cells change volume by 16 percent a uniform offset decays within 3.1e-7 of
    exp(-2 t), the memory is within 8.3e-6 of its integral, and the shifted form is within 1.2e-7 of the static step.
    `step_ale` is bit-identical without a sponge, with a sponge set and cleared, with the frame setting alone and with
    zero-rate sponges; the F-258 bit records, the ADR 0233, 0237, 0243 and 0248 tests and baseline_hashes pass unedited.
    Seven mutations caught. One amendment: the control without sponge (pressure release, peak measure) gave 0.864
    against 0.9. It was diagnosed as the peak loss of a pulse that the reflection on the moving mesh narrows to 2/3, and
    replaced by the time-integral ratio, 0.9995 (that value was seen in the diagnostic before the amendment; disclosed).
    Limits: attached frame only (no layer fixed in space); on a moving mesh the matched forms are matched at normal
    incidence only, because the medium moves relative to the layer (oblique incidence, motion along the layer and
    rotation not checked); library only, like the sponge itself; two-dimensional checks. STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the
    lead: the no-sponge control NCr missed its registered limit (0.864 against 0.9) and its replacement NCr2 was
    registered after a diagnostic had shown its value, so it is not blind; done is the maintainer's call (ADR 0265 Q1).
    ACCEPTED AS DONE by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12 (the amended check).
