    cells one ring outside the hole, which change kind as the cylinder passes (ADR 0359 event 2); the component cells
    fall by 4.22. Nine mutations caught. Not delivered: the case-tree wiring, BDF2 for step_sliding, replace_mesh and
    set_rest_conditions.
- [~] **F-346** Immersed solid: force and moment in unsteady flow
  - depends on: F-337
  - acceptance: The force and moment of an immersed solid subtract the rate of change of the momentum and angular
    momentum of its forced cells; DFG 2D-2 maximum drag and lift on M2 are within 1.5 percent of the FeatFlow level-6
    values, and a steady case returns the values of F-337 to round-off.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0249, 2026-11-12), in the library. From ADR 0239 question 3. The premise did not survive the
    derivation, written before any code: the reaction of the forcing is the discrete force on the staircase surface of
    the solid cells minus the storage of those cells, so for a body at rest it already is the force in unsteady flow,
    and the storage of the first fluid cells is fluid momentum that must not be removed; the storage that is not fluid
    momentum is that of the solid cells of a body whose rigid velocity changes in time. Delivered: rcfd-fv immersed.rs,
    `ImmersedForcing::force_moment_unsteady` (opt-in: the pair of `force_moment_second_order` plus the rate of change of
    the momentum and angular momentum held by the solid cells; `force_moment` and `force_moment_second_order` unchanged,
    hashes checked) and `immersed::velocity_rate` (the solvers' Euler and variable-step BDF2 difference; the caller
    keeps the older fields, no hunk in pimple.rs). Measured (limits registered before the code; three defective set-ups
    of the registration corrected by amendment 1 before their runs): the moment on a cylinder accelerated in a fixed
    outer one within 0.167 and 0.078 percent of the closed form at N 48 and 96 (limit 0.5; the reaction alone 4.3
    percent, the literal reading with the first fluid cells 1.8 and 0.9 percent); the force on an accelerated plate
    within 0.056 and 0.014 percent (limit 1; the reaction alone 42.8 percent, the literal reading 5.1 and 2.6 percent);
    a steady case returns F-337 exactly (2D-1 on M2 5.56246454, 0.0108880492; Couette by PISO); DFG 2D-2 against the
    recorded FeatFlow level-6 values, on M2 max C_D +0.261 %, max C_L -0.161 % (limit 1.5 %: met, but the old evaluation
    gives the same numbers, the two differ by 1.9e-6), on T (the mesh of ADR 0218) max C_D +0.815 %, max C_L +2.580 %
    (KNOWN MISS, predicted in the registration: not a storage term; the mean drag is +0.79 % and the steady 2D-1 lift on
    M2 +2.7 %; the two D/40 meshes differ by 2.7 points in the lift, so the M2 agreement is not shown to be
    convergence); nine mutations caught. Missing (why partial): the lift of 2D-2 on T; the unsteady evaluation as a
    default or behind a case key (open); the slivers between the staircase and the surface for an accelerating body;
    Crank-Nicolson and bounded BDF2 rates; moving shapes. Found on the way: 2D-2 on M2 with the second-order forcing of
    F-309 stops in PISO at step 6 (Courant 1.1e7), not diagnosed. Open: ADR 0249 Q1 (reword the first clause to the
    solid cells), Q2 (the 2D-2 clause: M2 as written, or replaced by the closed forms), Q3 (default). Follow-ups: F-354,
    F-355. ADR 0268 (2026-11-12, F-354) located the +2.58 percent lift of T: refining only the mesh around the cylinder
    to D/80 takes it to +0.02 percent; the -0.16 percent of M2 was a cancellation of that D/40 error by the coarse outer
    mesh; on the D/80 meshes both forcings are within 0.43 percent.
- [ ] **F-347** Vendor heat-flux card for the structural load deck from a cited open specification
  - depends on: F-237
  - acceptance: A specification of the card (fields, sign, required surface elements) from an open source is placed in
    the repository; the deck writes it beside RCFDQ; the tube heat rate after a round trip through the repository reader
    matches the fluid heat rate to 0.1 percent
  - note: Priority P3. Size S. Area: io. Opened by ADR 0244: RCFDQ is the repository's own card; no vendor heat-flux
    card layout is specified in the repository, so none was written. NEEDS THE USER: an open specification of the card
    has to be placed in the repository first (clean-room rule).
- [~] **F-348** Anisotropic (directional) refinement: a lattice with per-axis levels
  - depends on: F-343
  - acceptance: A lattice with per-axis refinement levels gives valid closed meshes for random directional marks
    (validate, closure, volume) and transfers linear fields exactly; on the ADR 0247 suction layer a directional run
    reaches the isotropic adapted error E(A) with at most half of its 3841 cells; the isotropic AmrMesh paths stay bit
    for bit.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0267, 2026-11-12): rcfd_mesh::adapt::aniso::AnisoMesh, a second lattice with one refinement level
    per axis (AxisLeaf, AxisMark; AmrMesh untouched): faces are the intersections of the sides of two leaves, with the
    corners of all face rectangles in the vertex set, so cells are closed for any tiling by dyadic boxes; optional
    balance of one level per refined axis across every face (at most 2 faces per side in a slab, 4 in 3-D); the existing
    Transfer and transfer_field. Random directional marks on a graded 3-D box, a slab and a box refined along two of
    three axes give valid closed meshes (validate, closure and volume to 1e-13) and linear fields transfer to 4.4e-16;
    on isotropic marks the mesh, the transfer and the adaptive loop equal AmrMesh's bit for bit. Directional criterion
    in rcfd_fv::adaptive (axis_variations, directional_axes with theta = 1/2, directional_target_marks,
    run_adaptive_simple_directional and _target). On the ADR 0247 suction layer the directional run has error 0.00298
    with 1547 cells against the isotropic 0.01159 with 3841 (limit: at most 1920 cells); held at the isotropic finest
    size it reaches 0.01158 with 960 cells; with the axis choice inverted 1.18. ADR 0054, 0242 and 0247 tests pass
    unedited (the heavy ones included); ten mutations each failed their tests. Partial by the rule because two
    registered supporting checks missed and were corrected under amendments: pair coarsening in 3-D can leave a five-box
    tiling of a cell that it cannot merge further (valid mesh; slabs return to the base), and the fast layer test on an
    8 x 8 base (cell Peclet 10) had no converged solution on its first directional mesh (replaced by a 16 x 16 base).
    Open: a box merge for 3-D coarsening (R2), the case key (R5), cells spent along x in early cycles (R4). Follow-ups:
    F-438 (case key), F-439 (three-dimensional box merge). The box merge is delivered by F-439 (ADR 0341, 2026-11-12):
    repeated all-axes box coarsening returns any state, the five-box tiling included, to the base.
- [~] **F-349** Overset: the response to the truncation of the background-fringe interpolation
  - depends on: F-334
  - acceptance: The response R_b of ADR 0246 (the difference of the RL runs with the library stencils and with a
    third-order interpolation on the background fringe: 4.87e-5, 2.19e-5, 1.41e-5 at levels 1 to 3, orders 1.153 and
    1.093) is traced to a named term of the coupled step by a switch that brings its order to 1.7 or more on levels 1 to
    4, or is shown to reach order 1.7 on finer levels or at a later time, or the ADR names why not with a number.
  - note: From ADR 0246 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR
    0340, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL, a diagnosis, tests only, no library change. No clause of the order check is met. R_b (the
    library's quadratic donor interpolation of F-336 on the background fringe against the default stencils; within 2.5
    percent of ADR 0246) is 4.996e-5, 2.177e-5, 1.412e-5, 8.917e-6, 6.425e-6 at t = 0.5 on levels 1 to 5, orders 1.198,
    1.068, 1.598, 1.469; run on to t = 3 on levels 1 to 3 it is 1.403e-4, 5.250e-5, 3.376e-5, orders 1.418, 1.089, and
    still growing; half the time step changes it by under 1 percent. Found on the way: the truncation of the background
    fringe of RL alternates between odd and even levels (coefficient 0.0685, 0.0781, 0.0621, 0.0693, 0.0638; the
    reflection of the fringe phase is not a symmetry), so orders between successive levels of RL carry a factor 1.26;
    within the parity families R_b has 1.150, 1.288, 1.542. On a set-up locked exactly, with equal spacings and no
    modulation along the ring (RE), the truncation converges at 1.995, 1.956 and R_b at 0.983, 1.015: the response per
    unit of truncation is proportional to the level (0.168, 0.339, 0.497) with no levelling off. Ruled out with numbers:
    a time-step or splitting term, a late settling at second order, the unequal spacings and the modulation. Named and
    confirmed: the normal velocity of a fringe cell is imposed softly. The flux of a face between a calculated and a
    fringe cell is that of the pressure equation with the interpolated fringe pressure and differs from the
    face-interpolated velocity by a defect D held by a pressure jump dJ = -(16 nu / 3 h) D (measured face by face on RE:
    0.9986, 1.0162 of that, correlation 0.995, 0.999), a resistance proportional to nu / h. The calculated cell across a
    fringe face follows a change of the normal fringe velocity by 0.51, 0.66, 0.76, 0.79, 0.83 at the background fringe
    (levels 1 to 5, t = 0.5; 0.10 to 0.51 at t = 0.025) and by 0.34 to 0.83 at the component fringe; each fringe costs
    about half an order on these levels. Refining the background alone raises R_b. Not shown: the level or time at which
    R_b reaches 1.7, and a formula for R_b from the resistance. One registered kinematic check missed (the truncation
    order between levels 3 and 4, 1.621 against 1.8, the alternation) and is kept as a known miss. Controls held, five
    mutations caught. Follow-up (ADR 0340 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of
    2026-11-11): an opt-in that prescribes the flux of the calculated-fringe faces from the interpolated velocity. ADR
    0347 (F-445), 2026-11-12: with the flux of the fringe faces prescribed and the pressure gradient of the neighbouring
    calculated cells taken from their own part, the order of R_b is 1.962, 1.789 on RE and 2.704, 2.124 within the
    parity families of RL: removing the soft imposition named here restores the order. The response is then larger on
    the levels run (R_b 9.0 to 3.3 times), because the interpolation error is handed on in full.
- [~] **F-350** Strong body-flow coupling selectable from the case tree
  - depends on: F-251
  - acceptance: A case with dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling = "strong" (default "loose") and its relaxation, added-mass
    estimate, tolerance, force scale and iteration cap as keys runs the spring-mounted piston at a mass ratio of 4
    through the case driver and reproduces ADR 0250 S1 to S3 (omega within 2 percent, no growth of same-side turning
    points over 10 periods, dt halving within 0.5 percent), the same case with coupling = "loose" stops with a located
    error or grows; a step that reaches the cap stops the run with a located message unless a key says to continue;
    every static check of the new keys is located; with the default every existing case hash is bit-identical.
  - note: From ADR 0250 questions 2 and 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11.
    PARTIAL (ADR 0266, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment): the optional table
    [dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling] (absent from every case that does not write it; a key inside the existing table
    six_dof would need an entry in the H1 hash table, so the acceptance's coupling = "strong" is written scheme =
    "strong" in that table) selects the strong coupling of rcfd_fv::fsi::strong_step in the case driver; keys scheme
    (loose default, strong), relaxation (aitken default, fixed), added_mass (the factor 2M/(2M + m')), tolerance,
    force_scale, moment_scale, max_iterations, at_cap (stop default, continue). Tree runs equal strong_step called
    directly bit for bit (60 steps with ADR 0250's settings, 40 with a fixed factor and every key away from its
    default). The spring-mounted piston of ADR 0250 at mass ratio 4 through the case driver gives ADR 0250's numbers to
    their printed digits: omega_m/omega 1.005081 at T/100 (limit 2 %), dt halving 1.7e-5 (limit 0.5 %), largest ratio of
    same-side turning points 0.92452 and 0.96141 over 11 crossings (never grows), 3.0 flow solves a step; with scheme =
    "loose" (or no table) it passes 10 X at step 28 (T/100) and 31 (T/200) and stops at steps 34 and 40 with a located
    mesh error. A step at the cap stops the run with "dynamic_mesh: step N, t = ...:
    dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling.max_iterations: ..."; with at_cap = "continue" the run goes on with one warning event,
    and the cap 1 equals the loose run bit for bit. Every static check of the new keys is located at its key (strong
    with a prescribed motion, rest patches or Newmark; tolerance, scales, added mass, cap; unknown values and keys).
    Without the table nothing changes: baseline hashes, case_hashes_w48u, the K0 tests of ADR 0257 and 0262 and the
    dynamic_mesh tree tests pass unedited; a table with scheme = "loose" equals no table bit for bit. The one mutation
    of ADR 0266 that passed its named test (force_scale not read; the floor k X was inert in E1 because moment_scale = 0
    makes the moment term the unfloored force ratio) is caught by the binding-floor test of ADR 0349 (F-437,
    2026-11-12); proposed done by ADR 0349 Q1. Done is the maintainer's call (ADR 0349 Q1 recommends done). Open: ADR
    0266 Q1 (status), Q2 (the key name), Q3 (Newmark), Q4 (rest patches). The wall pressure of the body force stays the
    default extrapolation (F-358). Follow-up: F-437. The key naming (Q2: scheme = "strong" in the table
    [dynamic_mesh.six_dof.coupling]) accepted by the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12.
- [x] **F-351** Wall pressure of the body force on a fixed-flux moving wall (the 1.25 percent added-mass deficit)
  - depends on: F-251, F-244
  - acceptance: The cause of the discrete added mass of the piston column lying 1.25 percent below rho A L0 (ADR 0250 C1
    and S1, ADR 0211 B1) is identified by a test that separates the wall-pressure extrapolation of patch_force_moment
    from the pressure of the flow step; if it is the extrapolation, an opt-in evaluation that uses the prescribed
    pressure gradient of the wall brings the sub-iteration gain at ratio 4 within 0.2 percent of the 2.977 of the model
    and omega_m/omega within 0.1 percent of 1 on the 20-cell column, and the convergence of the deficit with the cell
    size is shown on 20, 40 and 80 cells; the default force evaluation is unchanged unless the maintainer approves the
    change with its effect on the existing hashes listed.
  - note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0250 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's
    standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE (ADR 0252, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, four amendments). Cause,
    measured: the wall-pressure extrapolation of patch_force_moment. Its least-squares gradient (weights 1/d^2) takes
    the stored zero-gradient wall value of the pressure field as a data point with the weight of the neighbour cell,
    while the pressure equation of the moving-mesh step used the prescribed gradient -n . a_wall; the gradient of the
    wall cell is therefore exactly half (0.5 to 1e-16) and the wall pressure a quarter cell short: the force is low by
    1/(4N), first order in the cell size (prescribed piston, flow step converged: 1.2510e-2, 6.258e-3, 3.129e-3 on 20,
    40, 80 cells, orders 0.9993 and 0.9998), 1.25 percent on the 20-cell column at every mass ratio. The pressure of the
    flow step carries none of it (2e-6 with the step converged, 7e-6 with the registered two correctors). Delivered,
    opt-in, nothing calls it: sixdof::patch_force_moment_wall_gradient (the normal part of the cell-gradient
    extrapolation replaced by the gradient of ale::set_follow_conditions, p_c + dn g on an orthogonal wall cell, second
    order) and fsi::strong_step_with with fsi::WallPressure, which carries that gradient from step to step. With it:
    gain of the sub-iteration at ratio 4 2.97693 (model 2.977, limit 0.2 percent); omega_m/omega 1.000042 at ratio 4 on
    20, 40 and 80 cells (limit 0.1 percent; 1.005081, 1.002552, 1.001294 with the default), 0.999963 at ratio 20,
    1.000068 at 0.2, 1.000264 for the loose loop at 0.2 (1.001307 before: the unexplained +1.0e-3 of ADR 0211 was this
    deficit); deficit of the force 3e-6 on 20, 40, 80 cells. Every number equals the piston model with the exact added
    mass to six digits. Unchanged: patch_force_moment and strong_step (bit-identical over 40 steps; the sixdof,
    sixdof_coupled, sixdof_flow_f244 and strong_fsi_f251 suites pass unedited; baseline_hashes 3 passed, 0 failed, 1
    ignored (the file unedited)); pimple.rs, pimple/moving.rs, rcfd-api and the case schema untouched. Seven library
    mutations: six failed their checks; one added variant passed every test and a check (the gain at the third step of a
    run) was added by amendment and catches it. Disclosed: the first registered diagnosis missed its limits because its
    reference was the column of the new mesh; the pressure of the implicit Euler moving-mesh step is the acceleration
    times the column of the old mesh (first order in dt, not a mean deficit), and the reference was corrected by
    amendment after an exploration; the missed tests are kept as ignored records. Also found: the non-iterated step
    leaves a viscous splitting error that grows with the cell count and does not move the frequency. Not delivered: the
    case driver (rcfd-api dynmesh) still uses the default evaluation; a skewed wall cell and a moment in a flow are not
    tested. Open, the maintainer's: whether the prescribed gradient becomes the default (ADR 0252 Q1; not taken, it
    moves existing results), the case key (Q2), the audit of other walls with a prescribed gradient (Q3). Note of the
    lead: the acceptance limits were never changed, but the limits of the diagnosis were corrected by amendment 2 after
    a run and a prints-only exploration, so they were set with numbers seen. Follow-up (ADR 0252 questions 1 to 3,
    recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-358. Open: question 1 (the
    prescribed gradient as the default changes existing hashes).
- [x] **F-352** Overset: donor search on cells with non-planar faces
  - depends on: F-134
  - acceptance: On the set-up B3d of ADR 0251 (two hexahedral parts whose interior points are displaced by up to 0.15 of
    the cell size in all three directions) every fringe centre gets a donor that agrees with a full search, the linear
    and the quadratic stencils reproduce linear and quadratic fields to 1e-11, and on meshes with planar faces the
    donors and stencils are bit-identical to those of today (the unit tests K2 and K4 of ADR 0219 and D1 of ADR 0251).
  - note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0251 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's
    standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0253, 2026-11-12: DONE. Derived: one plane for each face leaves no gap
    across a face but a sliver along every edge at which the planes of the four faces do not meet in one line, a gap or
    an overlap with equal chance, of cross-section at most (w_F + w_F')(w_G + w_G') for the warps w of the faces, second
    order in the warp; on B3d (warp up to 0.142 of the cell size) the estimate was 6e-4 of the volume each and 116 and
    114 of 200000 random points were measured in no cell and in two. Built in rcfd_mesh::overset: a cell with a face
    warped beyond the locator's tolerance (1e-10 of its box diagonal) is tested as the polyhedron of the triangles about
    its face centres, the same triangles from both sides of a face (triangulated_margin: the distance from the
    triangles, signed by the winding number, behind a bounding-box shortcut); a cell with planar faces keeps the plane
    test of ADR 0219 M3 unchanged; a point on a shared triangle goes to the lowest-numbered cell. Met: on B3d all 1069
    fringe centres get a donor equal to the full search and confirmed by an independent tetrahedral test, the linear
    stencils reproduce a linear field to 3e-16 and the quadratic stencils q3 to 9e-16 with no fallback; 250000 random
    points in the two warped parts each lie in exactly one cell; 39744 face centres and 12167 mesh points go to the
    lowest-numbered cell; on the planar set-ups (RL, TG_L, U, TR, DC, FB, B3, B3s) no cell is warped and the donors and
    default stencils equal those built from the rule of M3 bit for bit; K2, K4, D1, Q0 and the records R2 pass unedited.
    Cost: a search takes 4.5 microseconds on B3d, the connectivity 1.8 times that of B3. The present rule finds no cell
    for the fringe cells 16035 (as recorded) and 16245. Six mutations caught. Limits: kinematic only, one family of
    warped meshes; non-convex cells with planar faces keep the plane test. Open for the maintainer: whether every cell
    should use the triangulated test (it changes one donor of TR at a tie, ADR 0253 Q1). Follow-ups (ADR 0253 questions
    2 and 3, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-356, F-357. Open: question
    1 (the triangulated test for every cell changes one donor at a tie).
- [x] **F-353** Overset: the moving cylinder with the quadratic donor interpolation
  - depends on: F-336
  - acceptance: The set-up TR of ADR 0219 run with DonorInterpolation::Quadratic: mass of the domain and continuity
    within 1e-9, no fallback or the count reported, drag within 5 percent of the body-fitted run at every step from t =
    2 to t = 8 and the difference to the linear-stencil run reported; the ADR recommends for or against making the
    quadratic interpolation the default.
  - note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. From ADR 0251 question 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's
    standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR 0259, 2026-11-12: DONE (tests and ADR only, no library change). The set-up
    TR of ADR 0219 with DonorInterpolation::Quadratic over 400 steps: continuity 5.6e-17, net outflow 9.4e-15 of U D L,
    no fallback (156 stencils of nine cells at every step), no unconverged solve, drag within 5.86e-3 of the body-fitted
    run at every step from t = 2 to t = 8 (linear stencils 6.25e-3; the linear run and the body-fitted run reproduce ADR
    0219 to every printed digit). Against the linear run: C_D lower by 2.1e-4 on average (largest 1.6e-3), mean drag
    error 3.42e-3 against 3.21e-3, worse by more than 1e-4 at 164 of 301 steps; the step-to-step drag oscillation as the
    body crosses background cells halves (rms 0.98e-3 against 1.80e-3 of C_D); time 1.03 times. By the rule fixed before
    the run the ADR recommends against making the quadratic interpolation the default; the default stays the
    maintainer's decision (ADR 0259 Q1). Three mutations caught by the fast test.
- [~] **F-354** Immersed solid: DFG 2D-2 force extrema, mesh and time-step convergence
  - depends on: F-346
  - acceptance: DFG 2D-2 with the immersed cylinder is run on the T mesh and on T refined once (D/80, half the time
    step) and on M2 and M3; the maximum drag and lift on the finest mesh are within 1.5 percent of the FeatFlow level-6
    values and the error decreases from D/40 to D/80 on both families, or the part that does not converge (mesh of the
    wake, forcing order, outlet condition, time step) is identified by a registered measurement.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0268, 2026-11-12), measurement only, no library code. From ADR 0249 question 5. DFG 2D-2 with the
    immersed cylinder was run to t = 8 on T and on T refined once (T2, D/80, dt 5e-4) and on M2 and M3 (M3 also at dt
    5e-4), with `build` and with `build_second_order_bounded`, against the FeatFlow level-6 values. On the D/80 meshes
    max C_D and max C_L are within 0.43 percent with either forcing (T2 build +0.272/+0.325, T2 bounded +0.136/+0.175,
    M3 build +0.143/-0.283, M3 bounded +0.007/-0.429; St within 0.13 percent). The error decreases from D/40 to D/80 on
    the T family with build (lift 2.580 to 0.325), on the M family with the bounded form (1.011 to 0.429), and on the M
    family with build in the drag (0.261 to 0.143) but not in the lift (0.161 to 0.283, a known miss accounted for by
    the part measurements). Part measurements, each registered with its decision numbers: refining only the core around
    the cylinder on T takes the lift error from +2.69 to +0.02 percent, so the mesh at the cylinder carries the T
    anomaly; the rest of the mesh then moves it 0.31 point, halving the time step 0.11 (T) and 0.04 (M2) point, and
    moving the outlet from x = 2.2 to 4.4 changes nothing to six digits; the T and M families differ by 2.74 points of
    lift at D/40 and by 0.61 at D/80, so the M2 agreement of ADR 0249 was a cancellation between the D/40 core and the
    coarse outer mesh; the forcing order moves the extrema by up to 1.17 points at D/40 (M2) and at most 0.15 at D/80.
    Missing (why partial): T with the bounded forcing (D/40) stopped at step 2951 by the divergence guard, with pressure
    NaN in the pressure solve at the inlet corner cell, so the decrease on the T family with the bounded form is not
    formed; not diagnosed (library work). Open: ADR 0268 Q5 (the stop), Q6 (quote the D/80 values as the validation), Q7
    (status). ADR 0363 (2026-11-12, F-466): the stop of T with the bounded form was a breakdown of the
    AMG-preconditioned pressure CG at step 2951 (r^T z < 0, finite inputs); with the opt-in pressure_ic_fallback T runs
    to t = 8, max C_D +0.216 and max C_L +1.687 percent, so A2-T-2 is met (0.216 to 0.136, 1.687 to 0.175) and the
    forcing order on T moves the extrema by -0.60 and -0.89 point.
- [~] **F-355** Second-order immersed forcing: transient PISO at Re 100
  - depends on: F-309
  - acceptance: DFG 2D-2 on M2 with `build_second_order` runs to t = 8 in PISO with BDF2 and gives a Strouhal number
    within 1 percent of the first-order forcing on the same mesh, or the cause of the stop at step 6 is diagnosed by a
    registered measurement and the configuration is refused with a located message.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0254, 2026-11-12), in the library. From ADR 0249 question 6. The stop was reproduced (step 6,
    Courant 1.1094e7) and diagnosed by registered variant runs, each with its first-order control: it needs a
    fluid-solid face whose surface crossing lies close to the fluid cell centre, so that the linear extension of ADR
    0234 D1 has a weight above 5 (it multiplies the velocity of the first fluid cell relative to the wall by up to 38 on
    M2), together with the impulsive start; runs with weights of at most 5 (theta_min 0.1, 0.25, 0.5; mesh M1) and a run
    started from a developed field do not stop, and at each of the five steps the largest flux velocity sits on the face
    of weight 38.99 (2.49, 23, 1426, 9.2e4, 6.9e5). Ruled out, each by its number: the ddt flux correction, the
    corrector count, BDF2, the convection scheme, the time step (5e-4 to 8e-3 all stop) and the continuity of the fluid
    cells (7e-7). A hand estimate of a linear growth criterion (weight times the share of the time term in the diagonal)
    was refuted by its registered rule. Delivered: rcfd-fv immersed.rs, `ImmersedForcing::build_second_order_bounded`
    (opt-in): on the faces with a weight above 2 the flux is that of the wall value reflected through the image point of
    the face in the fluid, interpolated between the first fluid cell and the cell behind it, weights of magnitude at
    most 1, second order; `build` and `build_second_order` are bit-identical (three hashes, the existing immersed tests,
    baseline_hashes). With it DFG 2D-2 on M2 runs to t = 8 in PISO with BDF2: Strouhal number 0.30112 against 0.30041 of
    the first-order forcing (+0.24 percent, limit 1), C_D max -0.33 percent and C_L max -1.01 percent of FeatFlow;
    circular Couette error 5.91e-3, 1.63e-3, 4.23e-4, order 1.947 (limit 1.5), PISO equal to SIMPLEC to 0.1 percent.

    and can return more than the time term carries (`flux_growth`; 2D-2 on M2 at step 1, value 2.2; the runs of ADR 0234
    and 0249 are not refused); the refusal is a sufficient condition, not a stability criterion (time steps of 4e-3 and
    8e-3 still stop by the Courant guard). Seven mutations caught. Partial by the registered rule because of two known
    misses: the flux velocity after the first step was registered as at least 4.5 and is 2.49 (the growth builds over
    steps 2 to 5), and the bounded form with a single PISO corrector stops at step 34 (any flux face that returns the
    wall-normal velocity at full size does, with one corrector; with two or more it runs). Acceptance: the second branch
    (diagnosis and located refusal) is met; the first is met with the bounded opt-in, not with `build_second_order` as
    named. Open (ADR 0254 questions 1 to 3): whether `build_second_order` should build the bounded form (changes
    recorded numbers of ADR 0234 and 0239), the form of the refusal, the single corrector. Not run: M3, T, three
    dimensions, PIMPLE outer iterations, SIMPLE with under-relaxation. Follow-ups: F-363 (the single corrector), F-364
    (the bounded form as build_second_order; needs the maintainer). ADR 0268 (2026-11-12, F-354):
    `build_second_order_bounded` ran 2D-2 to t = 8 on T2 and M3 (D/80, within 0.43 percent of FeatFlow) but stopped on T
    (D/40, dt 1e-3) at step 2951, with pressure NaN in the pressure solve at the inlet corner cell; not diagnosed. ADR
    0363 (2026-11-12, F-466): the stop of build_second_order_bounded on T (ADR 0268) is not a stop of the forcing but of
    the AMG-preconditioned pressure CG (r^T z < 0 at step 2951); with the opt-in PimpleSettings::pressure_ic_fallback
    the run reaches t = 8. ADR 0374 (2026-11-12, F-363): with one PISO corrector a flux face with an image or a weight
    above 1 is refused at step 1 with a located message; the stop of the bounded form with one corrector (step 34)
    depends on the time step (it runs at dt 5e-4 and 2.5e-4) and is not explained by the pressure-lag map.

- [x] **F-360** Co-simulation protocol over the solver service
  - depends on: F-139, F-085
  - acceptance: The calls of docs/cosimulation-protocol.md (describe, time, checkpoint, restore, forces, advance) are
    served by the JSON-RPC service under a new protocol version; an out-of-process mock structural participant driven
    over TCP reproduces ADR 0256 A1 and A2 (every step converged, omega_m/omega within 0.5 percent and 3 percent) and
    the same displacements as the in-process run to 1e-12; a dropped connection or a participant error stops the step
    with a located error and both sides restored; the protocol document is versioned; existing service tests and case
    hashes are unchanged.
  - note: Merged 2026-11-12. DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0345, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, two amendments).
    The calls of docs/cosimulation-protocol.md are served by the JSON-RPC service for participants that the embedding
    program hosts (rcfd_api::cosim_service: Service::host_fluid, host_structure, each participant on its own thread so
    it need not be Send; rcfd serve hosts none; no case key, CLI or MCP change): methods cosim.list, cosim.open,
    cosim.describe, cosim.time, cosim.checkpoint, cosim.restore, cosim.forces, cosim.advance, plain JSON numbers that
    cross bit for bit (serde_json float_roundtrip), error codes 1005 (the participant error, its own message) and 1006
    (no such participant). Service protocol 1.1: the identifier rcfd-service/1 is kept (the pinned tests are unedited),
    service.info gains protocol_version 1.1 and cosim rcfd-cosim/1; both protocol pages are versioned. The coupler is
    the unchanged cosim::coupled_step driven with the proxies RemoteStructure and RemoteFluid (TCP). A lease per
    participant (cosim.open) refuses requests left over from an old connection; a proxy whose connection is lost fails
    at once except restore, which reconnects once and restores the participant, so a dropped connection ends the step
    with the located error and both sides at the start of the step. Measured on the model problem of ADR 0256 with the
    mock structure in a second process: every one of 650 steps converged, 7 to 10 iterations (mean 8.766), omega_m/omega
    0.998618 and 1.011453, and the displacements of every node at every step equal to the in-process run bit for bit
    (limit 1e-12 X), also with both participants remote (100 steps); a participant error (structure in the other
    process, fluid hosted) and a dropped connection (cut before the request, after the reply, between steps, fluid or
    structure) each give an error naming participant, time and iteration with 0 bits of either state changed and the
    next step equal to the reference; a killed participant process gives the located error in 2.1 s with the fluid
    restored and the failed reconnection reported; refusals with their codes; a control with springs stiffer by 1e-9 is
    seen (4e-9 X). Amendment 1: the first transport cost 2 ms per call (lines written in pieces), now 0.05 ms (one write
    per line, TCP_NODELAY on accepted connections; no byte changes). Amendment 2: the 650-step out-of-process tests are
    ignored heavy records (minutes on the loaded machine; run twice, identical), the gate runs the 100-step both-remote
    comparison and the failure tests. Existing service, CLI and MCP suites and the case hashes pass unedited; seven
    mutations each failed their tests. Not delivered: participants built from a case or hosted by rcfd serve, structural
    elements in describe, authentication, a test of a call outlasting the time-out. Open: ADR 0345 Q1 to Q5. Follow-up
    F-444 (ADR 0380, 2026-11-12): participants from the case hosted by rcfd serve --cosim, elements in describe, one
    write per service::Client request (ADR 0345 Q3, Q4, Q5).
- [x] **F-361** Quasi-Newton acceleration of the coupled iteration
  - depends on: F-139
  - acceptance: A least-squares (quasi-Newton) update of the nodal force from the residual history of the step, opt-in
    beside the fixed and Aitken factors, converges the model problem of ADR 0256 to 1e-8 in at most 7 iterations per
    step and 6 or fewer on average (Aitken: 8.8), gives the same frequencies within 1e-6, and with one rigid node needs
    no more iterations than Aitken; registered before the run with the plain fixed point as the diverging control.
  - note: DONE pending acceptance (ADR 0261, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, no amendment). Opt-in
    fsi::Relaxation::LeastSquares { initial, filter } (CouplingSettings::least_squares) in cosim::coupled_step: after a
    first update relaxed with initial, the next nodal force is the flow's force plus the combination of the step's
    output differences whose residual differences best cancel the current residual (interface quasi-Newton with a
    least-squares inverse Jacobian), solved by Householder QR newest column first with a filter that drops a column
    whose part outside the newer ones is below 1e-2 of its norm (no vanishing pivot); no reuse across steps;
    fsi::strong_step refuses it. Derived: on a linear map it is GMRES plus one pass, exact at iteration d + 2. Measured
    on the model problem of ADR 0256 (6 nodes, 16 faces, tolerance 1e-8): every one of 650 steps converged, at most 7
    iterations (one step), mean 5.980 (Aitken 8.766, histogram identical to ADR 0256), frequencies equal to Aitken's
    within 3.1e-10; one rigid node (SPm1): the same 301 iterations as Aitken, the same count in every step, positions
    bit-identical; the plain fixed point diverges (510.85 in 10). Mock affine and cubic fluids check the termination
    count and the equality with Aitken's secant. Existing suites cosim_f139, strong_fsi_f251, added_mass_f351 and the
    baseline hashes pass unedited; four mutations caught. Open: ADR 0261 Q1 to Q3.
- [x] **F-362** Interface mapping by geometric search and radial-basis functions, with an unmapped-value policy
  - depends on: F-139
  - acceptance: InterfaceMap weights are built from the two interface meshes alone (nearest-element projection and a
    radial-basis interpolation) for a planar and a cylindrical wall with non-matching meshes; rigid translation and
    rotation are reproduced to 1e-12, resultant force, moment and work are conserved to 1e-12 by the transposed map, a
    wall point outside the structure is refused or mapped by a stated policy, and the model problem of ADR 0256 gives
    the same frequencies within 1e-3 with the built weights.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0263, 2026-11-12; registered before the code, one amendment after the registered run). Opt-in
    cosim::interface_rows and InterfaceMap::build build the weights from the structure's nodes and elements (points,
    segments, triangles, quadrilaterals) and the fluid's wall points alone; nothing calls them. Derived: scalar weights
    reproduce every rigid motion iff each row sums to 1 and reproduces the point's coordinates; the transpose then
    conserves resultant and moment, and conserves work for any weights. Nearest-element projection with an offset
    correction on the ring of elements (exact on a curved wall; plain barycentric selectable); radial basis with
    Wendland's C2 function of support 3 h and a degree-1 polynomial in the nodes' own directions, dense Cholesky with a
    Schur complement, condition estimate (8 to 85 here). Policy: a wall point farther than max_distance is refused (the
    default; the message names point and distance) or moves with its nearest structural point (Unmapped::Nearest).
    Measured on a planar and a cylindrical wall with non-matching meshes: rigid translation and rotation to 1.3e-15,
    resultant, moment and work to 1.4e-16 (both methods); without the correction the cylinder loses 5e-3 of the rotation
    and 1e-4 of the moment; outside points follow their nearest points to 9e-16 and the moment changes exactly as
    predicted. Model problem of ADR 0256: the projection gives the piecewise-linear rows to 1e-16 and the same
    frequencies (1.4e-15); the radial basis shifts them by -5.2e-4 and +1.9e-4 (limit 1e-3). cosim_f139, cosim_f361 and
    the baseline hashes pass unedited; eight mutations caught. Partial because the registered check E1 accepted two
    coincident nodes with the radial basis (an absolute pivot test); amendment 1 refuses pivots below 2 n eps a_jj, and
    E1b passes with it. Protocol option in docs/cosimulation-protocol.md. Open: ADR 0263 Q1 to Q3. ACCEPTED AS DONE by
    the maintainer in person on 2026-11-12 (the amended check).

    forcing, 1.248 for the bounded form), below one by step 11 for both (0.977, 0.988); it is not caused by the pressure
    solve and does not predict the stop. ADR 0392 (2026-11-13, F-482): a finite-difference linearisation of the whole

    body); from a projected start without flow through the cylinder it runs 200 steps (max abs(u) 2.208). ADR 0425

    cut-off (36, 23), pair splits 2.8e-13, expanded-mode residual 8.2e-12 (limit 1e-7) and M-orthonormality 2.3e-15;
    thin ring t/R = 0.05, nu = 0: n = 2 at k = 2 within 4.4e-4, n = 3 at k = 3 within 1.8e-3 (limit 2 percent); spinning
    annular disc b/a = 4, nu = 0.3: rim displacement within 8.9e-5 of rho omega^2 b ((3 + nu) a^2 + (1 - nu) b^2)/(4E)
    (derived; agrees with the roadmap; limit 1 percent), sector statics equal to the full disc within 3.3e-13. Refusals:
    unmatched boundaries with the first unmatched node, N < 2, k > N/2. Eight mutations caught. si_scaffold x1/r1-r9/r10
    after landed and si_mpc N5 kept as ignored records (maintainer decision 2026-11-13). Open, taken on the standing
    instruction: modal_analysis and solve_static on a model with a Cyclic constraint give the k = 0 result (documented).
    Follow-up F-489 (harmonic loads, rigid sets at k > 0).
- [~] **F-395** Geometric (initial-stress) stiffness of solid elements: pre-stressed modal analysis and linear buckling
  - depends on: F-388, F-374, F-376, F-382, F-383
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. K_sigma is symmetric within 1e-13
    of its norm, gives no force for a rigid translation within 1e-12, and for a uniform uniaxial stress s and a linear
    displacement field w gives x^T K_sigma x = s V |grad w . e|^2 within 1e-12. rcfd-linalg: for K = tridiagonal (2,
    -1), n = 200, and K_sigma = -I the ten lowest buckling factors equal 4 sin^2(j pi/(2 (n + 1))) within 1e-10; a
    K_sigma with no negative direction returns no factor and says so. Pre-stressed modes: a beam on knife-edge supports
    at its neutral axis (slenderness 20, nu = 0) under an axial tension stress s has (omega_n^2 - omega_n,0^2) = (n
    pi/L)^2 s/rho within 1 percent for n = 1 and 2, and under compression the frequency falls by the same amount.
    Buckling: the same beam in compression has the critical load pi^2 E I/L^2 reduced by the shear term (0.6 percent at
    this slenderness, registered) within 1 percent, the second factor four times the first within 2 percent; a
    clamped-free column pi^2 E I/(4 L^2) within 1 percent (Tet10 or Hex20).
  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290). ADR 0390, 2026-11-13: geometric stiffness of Tet4, Hex8,
    Tet10 and Hex20 (geometric::element_geometric_stiffness, Prestress from a static result, geometric_stiffness on the
    stiffness pattern, bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads), pre-stressed modes (geometric::prestressed_modes; a zero
    pre-stress has the bits of modal_analysis) and linear buckling (buckling::factors on
    rcfd_linalg::eigen::lowest_buckling_factors, subspace iteration on K^-1 (-K_sigma) verified by a Sturm count of K +
    s K_sigma; with no factor it returns the bound below which there is none). Symmetry 2.0e-16, translation 2.5e-16,
    uniaxial form 5.3e-15; tridiagonal factors 4.4e-15; frequency shifts 6.8e-4 and 2.4e-3 (tension), 5.0e-4 and 2.2e-3
    (compression); knife-edge buckling 2.0e-3 from Engesser (shear term 0.491 percent registered); clamped-free column
    1.7e-3. Known miss: the second factor is 2.0135e-2 from four times the first against 2e-2, because the solid's
    K_sigma also carries the axial stress on the rotating sections (r^2 k^2, the order of the shear term; the derived
    form matches within 1.7e-4). Transformation path (springs, linear constraints, rigid sets) refused. Follow-ups F-492
    (the knife-edge factors against the derived closed form), F-493 (transformation path). The A9 clause is settled by
    F-492 (ADR 0394): the solid's factors match the derived closed form within 1.7e-4, and at L/h = 40 the second factor
    is four times the first within 0.52 percent.
- [~] **F-396** Modes of a rotating part: stress stiffening by the centrifugal pre-stress, spin softening, Campbell diagram
  - depends on: F-395, F-375, F-383
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. At zero speed the result has the
    bits of the modal analysis of F-383. Radial bar clamped on the axis, nu = 0, axial modes: (omega_n,0^2 -
    omega_n^2)/Omega^2 = 1 within 1e-3 for n = 1, 2 at a speed with centrifugal stress below 1e-4 E. Radial beam of
    square section clamped on the axis (slenderness 20): the first out-of-plane (flap) and in-plane (lag) frequencies
    satisfy omega_flap^2 - omega_lag^2 = Omega^2 within 1e-4 Omega^2 on a symmetric mesh; the stiffening (omega_flap^2 -
    omega_0^2)/Omega^2 equals at Omega = 0.2 omega_0 the Rayleigh quotient of the centrifugal tension with the mode at
    rest (1.19, recomputed in the registration) within 2 percent and stays between 1 and that value up to Omega = 5
    omega_0. Campbell table: on a synthetic family omega^2 = omega_0^2 + S Omega^2 the crossings with orders 1 to 4
    equal omega_0/sqrt(k^2 - S) within 1e-8, and on the beam within 1 percent; a flap and a lag mode of a rectangular
    section that cross are tracked without exchange (modal assurance above 0.9). A speed at which K_eff is not positive
    definite is reported as a loss of stiffness with the speed, never as a non-finite frequency.
  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290). ADR 0403, 2026-11-13: rotating.rs gives the modes of a
    part spinning about an axis in the rotating frame, K + Omega^2 (K_sigma,1 - M_perp) with the centrifugal pre-stress
    of one static solve at 1 rad/s and the spin-softening mass m_ab (delta_ij - a_i a_j), on the elimination and the
    transformation path; speed 0 gives the bits of the modal analysis; a speed at which K_eff is not positive definite
    is reported as a loss of stiffness with the speed and the negative count (Sylvester inertia), never as a frequency;
    modes over speeds tracked by the mass-weighted modal assurance, engine-order crossings linear in Omega^2 (exact for
    omega^2 = omega_0^2 + S Omega^2, 2e-16), the Campbell table as CSV and JSON. Radial bar: spin softening 1 within
    1.9e-9, the full operator 1 - Q_n,h within 3.1e-5; square beam: stiffening 1.1907 at 0.2 omega_0 (2.2e-3 from
    1.1933), between 1 and the rest quotient up to 5 omega_0, crossings within 8.7e-6 of direct solves; flap and lag of
    a rectangular section tracked through their crossing (MAC 0.99999). Partial: the flap-lag identity misses 1e-4 at
    1.9e-3 (known miss, predicted in the registration): on a solid it is 1 - 2 f_x (met to 1.1e-8), f_x the axial
    kinetic share of the bending mode. Coriolis neglected. Follow-ups: the flap-lag clause restated for a solid,
    Coriolis coupling, rotating modes of a sector at a harmonic index. Follow-ups F-498 (flap-lag restated for a solid),
    F-499 (Coriolis), F-500 (cyclic sector at a harmonic index).
- [~] **F-397** Geometric nonlinearity: total Lagrangian solid elements, Newton iteration with load steps
  - depends on: F-395, F-374, F-375
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The tangent agrees with central

    element size (registered seed). A rigid rotation by 90 degrees with a translation gives an internal force below
    1e-10 E L^2. Uniform stretch lambda = 1.2 of a bar with nu = 0: nominal stress E lambda (lambda^2 - 1)/2 within
    1e-9; under load control the last three residuals of each step show an order >= 1.8. A load factor of 1e-6
    reproduces the linear solution within 1e-5 relative. Elastica: a cantilever of slenderness 50, nu = 0, with tip
    force P L^2/(E I) = 1 and 2 has the tip deflection and shortening within 2 percent of the elliptic-integral solution
    (recomputed in the registration by integrating the elastica equation; recalled 0.302 L, 0.056 L and 0.494 L, 0.161
    L). An element inverted during the iteration and a step that does not converge after the registered halvings are
    errors with the element or the step.
  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-13). Size M. ADR 0404, 2026-11-13 (registration
    of stub ADR 0300): nonlinear::solve, total Lagrangian Tet4, Hex8, Tet10 and Hex20 with St. Venant-Kirchhoff, tangent
    K_mat(F) + K_sigma(S) (the geometric stiffness of ADR 0390), Newton with load steps, residual and energy criteria,
    step halving, inversion and non-convergence refused naming the element or the step; Element::internal_force and

    stretch nominal stress 1e-16, order 2.02 to 2.08, elastica within 2.4e-4 to 5.8e-4 of the ODE (limit 2e-2). Partial:
    the linear limit (load factor 1e-6) missed in its registered run (cancellation in F^T F - I; met after amendment 1

    for the maintainer (ADR 0404 question 1): count A5 as met after amendment 1. Follow-up F-497.
- [~] **F-398** Linear transient dynamics: Newmark and generalised-alpha integration, Rayleigh damping, load histories
  - depends on: F-388, F-373, F-374, F-383
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Free vibration started in the first
    axial mode of a bar (the discrete eigenvector): with Newmark the amplitude after 100 periods is within 1e-9 and the
    total energy constant within 1e-10; the measured period is long by (omega dt)^2/12 within 5 percent of that amount
    at omega dt = 0.2 and 0.1, observed order >= 1.9. A step load proportional to M phi_1 gives the peak displacement
    twice the static one within 0.5 percent at 40 steps per period. Rayleigh damping with a registered ratio 0.02 on
    that mode: logarithmic decrement 2 pi zeta/sqrt(1 - zeta^2) within 1 percent. Generalised-alpha: with spectral
    radius 1 the result equals Newmark within 1e-12; with 0.5 and 0.8 a mode at omega dt = 1e3 decays per step by that
    factor within 1e-3 while the period error of the first mode keeps order >= 1.9. A run split in two by save and
    restore has the bits of the unsplit run; results are bit-identical for 1 and 8 threads; a non-positive step, a table
    that does not cover the run and a singular effective matrix are refused.
  - note: ADR 0389, 2026-11-13: rcfd-fem transient::Integrator: Newmark (beta, gamma; average acceleration by default)
    and generalised-alpha (rho_inf, parameters re-derived: triple root -rho_inf at infinity), Rayleigh damping
    (from_ratio), piecewise linear LoadTable with exact coverage checks, LoadHistory patterns, one factor of the
    effective matrix, initial acceleration from M, state saved and restored as bytes (RCFDTRS1). Bar of 20 Hex8:
    amplitude after 100 periods 9e-15, energy 2.5e-14, period error 0.9974 and 0.9993 of (omega dt)^2/12, order 1.997;
    step-load peak 1.0e-5 from twice static; Rayleigh 0.02 decrement 1.7e-3; rho_inf = 1 equals Newmark to 1.6e-14;
    split run and 1/8 threads bit-equal; the three refusals and 16 more. Known miss A8: the method decays at omega dt =

    radius within 1e-6 at omega dt = 1e3 and rho_inf within 1e-3 at 1e6 (A8c, A8d, both met), which would make the item
    done. Follow-up F-490.

- [~] **F-400** Dynamic solid as a co-simulation participant, on interface weights built from the two surfaces
  - depends on: F-398, F-139, F-361, F-362, F-385
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A bar (nu = 0) whose end face is
    the interface, coupled by coupled_step to a mock fluid that returns the force -m_a times the wall acceleration: the
    first coupled frequency equals the root of k L tan(k L) = rho A L/m_a within 1 percent at 100 steps per period, for
    mass ratios m_a/(rho A L) of 0.5 and 4; at ratio 4 the plain iteration (factor 1) diverges as the protocol predicts
    (registered control) while Aitken's factor and the least-squares update converge to 1e-8 within registered iteration
    caps. With a mock spring k_f and a slow load the response tends to F_0/(k_s + k_f) of F-385 within 1e-6. Mapping
    built by F-362 for a matching and for a 3:2 non-matching interface: resultant force, moment and work conserved
    within 1e-12, and the coupled frequency changes by less than 1e-3 between the two. Restore returns the checkpoint
    bit for bit; a failing structural step stops the coupled step with the participant's name and both sides restored.
    No flow solver is coupled.
  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290). PARTIAL (ADR 0410, 2026-11-13; registered before the
    code, amendment 1 after the registered run, amendment 2 after the mutations). rcfd_post::solid_dynamic::DynamicSolid
    implements cosim::Structure on the transient integrator of ADR 0389/0393 (Newmark or generalised-alpha, either
    path): advance holds the interface forces over one or more sub-steps through the new opt-in
    Integrator::run_with_force (the force added at both ends of every step, reduced like a load pattern; run and step
    keep their bits), checkpoint and restore keep the integrator's state and the held forces bit for bit, elements gives
    the surface set's faces to the map builders; no dependency edge added (rcfd-post already depends on rcfd-fv and
    rcfd-fem), rcfd-fv::cosim unchanged. Bar 4 x 1 x 1 m, Hex8 20 x 2 x 2, nu = 0, clamped, end face the interface,
    coupled by coupled_step to a test-only piston mock (one wall acceleration, Newmark-consistent, force -m_a a) at 100
    steps per period: first coupled frequency against the root of k L tan(k L) = rho A L/m_a 2.8e-4 (ratio 0.5) and
    3.3e-4 (ratio 4) (limit 1 %), against the discrete Newmark prediction 1.5e-7; the plain iteration diverges with the
    derived slope -m_a e^T S^{-1} e (-59.69 at ratio 4) to 6e-16; Aitken and least squares converge to 1e-8 in 3
    iterations per step on the matching and the 3:2 map built by F-362; spring 1.5 k_s with a slow load
    (generalised-alpha rho_inf = 0) to F_0/(k_s + k_f) within 1.1e-10; resultant, moment and work conserved to 2.2e-16;
    restore bit for bit; a failing structural step (load table, non-finite force) stops the step naming 'solid' in
    iteration 1 and 2 with both sides restored. Partial: the coupled frequency changes by 6.3e-3 (ratio 4) and 2.4e-3
    (ratio 0.5) between the matching and the 3:2 map (limit 1e-3; diagnosed: the transposed projection loads the 2 x 2
    face with non-consistent weights, 1.5 % more static compliance; a known-miss record). The registered per-face
    added-mass mock made the coupled run unstable (non-uniform patterns with slopes of hundreds below the convergence
    test grow by about 700 per step); amendment 1 made the mock a piston. Eight mutations caught (one after amendment
    2). Baseline hashes pass. No flow solver is coupled. Open: ADR 0410 Q1 to Q3. Follow-up: F-NEW (frequency change
    against the face refinement and the map). Follow-up F-502. The frequency change between the maps (M2c, 6.3e-3) is
    the extra static compliance of the mapped weights; its dependence on the face refinement and the map is measured by
    F-502 (ADR 0412, 2026-11-13): below 1e-3 from 8 x 8 elements with the projection and from 4 x 4 with the radial
    basis. The added-mass growth of the per-face mock (amendment 1) does not occur with the flow solver: in F-401 (ADR
    0434, 2026-11-14) the non-uniform part of the interface force stays at rounding on the matching wall and decays on
    the 3:2 wall, its slopes being those of the local flow, far below 1.
- [~] **F-401** Two-way coupling of an elastic solid with the incompressible flow solver: the piston on an elastic bar
  - depends on: F-400, F-251, F-351, F-361, F-362
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Elastic bar (nu = 0) closing a
    channel of incompressible fluid of length L_f, started from a displaced state, mass ratios rho_f L_f/(rho_s L_s) of
    0.5 and 4: the coupled iteration converges in every step to 1e-6 with Aitken's factor and with the least-squares
    update, iteration counts recorded; the frequency of the first coupled mode equals the root of k L tan(k L) = rho_s
    L_s/(rho_f L_f) within 2 percent after the registered estimate of the time-step and viscous effects; over ten
    periods the work of the fluid on the interface equals the change of the solid's energy within 1e-4 of its amplitude;
    the loose coupling (one pass) at ratio 4 grows (registered control). With a 3:2 non-matching interface mapped by
    F-362 the frequency changes by less than 2e-3. A failure of either participant leaves both at the start of the step.
    The existing co-simulation tests (cosim_f139, cosim_f361, cosim_f362) pass unedited.
  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290). PARTIAL (ADR 0434, 2026-11-14; registered before the
    code, amendment 1 after the first run). The elastic bar of F-400 (DynamicSolid, Hex8 20 x 4 x 4, nu = 0, clamped,
    L_s = 4 m) closes a channel of incompressible fluid (FlowWall, moving-mesh PISO with the prescribed wall gradient of
    F-351, slip side walls, open end, L_f = 32 m), coupled by coupled_step at mass ratios rho_f L_f/(rho_s L_s) of 0.5
    and 4 from the static release of a tip traction (solid and fluid start consistent, at rest);
    rcfd_post::solid_fsi::ChannelMotion moves the channel mesh with the axial interface displacement. Over 1001 steps at
    T/100: Aitken and the least-squares update converge to 1e-6 in 3 iterations every step on the matching wall and in 4
    to 12 on a 3:2 wall (bilinear projection of F-504 on a 4 x 4 face); the first coupled frequency is the root of k L
    tan(k L) = rho_s L_s/(rho_f L_f) to 1.6e-4 (0.5) and 1.1e-3 (4), and the discrete model of the pairing (the Newmark
    bar with the plug force of the flow step, one step of lag: the registered time-step estimate) to 4e-7 (limit 2
    percent after the estimate); over ten periods the fluid's work on the interface equals the change of the solid's
    energy to 5e-6 of its amplitude (limit 1e-4); the loose coupling at ratio 4 grows by 13.8 per step; the 3:2 wall
    changes the frequency by 8.2e-4 (4) and 3.1e-4 (0.5) (limit 2e-3; ADR 0414's piston mock gave 8.18e-4); a failing
    solid (load table) or fluid (mesh motion) stops the step naming it, both sides bit-equal to the start of the step.
    The non-uniform part of the interface force (ADR 0410 Q3) stays at 1e-9 of the force on the matching wall and decays
    over the run on the 3:2 wall (at most 8.8e-4): with a real column its slopes are far below 1, so the growth seen
    with F-400's per-face mock does not occur. Partial: the registered viscous estimate 0 is wrong in kind (the PISO
    step's viscous splitting moves the tip by 8.3e-5 U at nu x 100, proportional to nu; a known miss, below 1e-6 in
    frequency at the case's viscosity), and the helper check H1 was met only after amendment 1 (a limit below the
    coordinate's resolution). Six mutations caught. No line of rcfd-fv or rcfd-api changed. Open: ADR 0434 Q1 to Q3. ADR
    0446 (F-421, 2026-11-14) found that Symmetry planes add a dissipation to a flow tangential to them in the PISO step
    (+7 to +13 percent of the viscous impedance of an oscillating channel); this may be the cause of the VS miss of ADR
    0434 (not tested). Re-check under F-531. ADR 0455 (F-531, 2026-11-14): the VS miss is the averaged component
    diagonal of the PISO correctors next to the four Symmetry side walls; with PimpleSettings::component_diagonal = true
    VS is 1.0e-10 U (limit 1e-6 U).

  - note: Structural solver, intermediate tier (plan ADR 0290, 2026-11-12). ADR 0305, 2026-11-12:
    rcfd_linalg::amg_elastic (new, beside the untouched scalar AMG): smoothed aggregation on the node-block graph (theta

    0.2 grew 6 times by t = 1.5, where at rest it stays at 0.30. Built (rcfd-fv):
    `sponge::SpongeFrame::AttachedWithLabMemory`, with the rates attached to the cells and the memories of the matched

    is the matched layer at rest. Measured: a plane pulse with a smooth envelope along its front (the solver has no
    periodic condition, and the moving boundaries exclude a mirror wall), through the layer of ADR 0237 on grids
    translating along it at Mach 0.2, reflects 1.6e-4 at 30 degrees and 3.5e-4 at 45 degrees (2.7e-4 and 3.6e-4 at rest;
    limit 1e-2) and stays bounded over 20 transit times of the layer (largest amplitude the incident peak). The F-341
    frame reflects 7.2e-3 and 3.2e-2 in the same runs. It did not blow up within 20 transit times there, although the
    one-dimensional check shows the instability. A plain radial layer on a rotating O-grid, Mach 0.2 at the layer,
    reflects 2.8e-3 of an outgoing cylindrical pulse, as at rest; the plain form reflects about w/(8r) of a cylindrical
    pulse, which comes from the geometry. The transport matches a closed form to 1.9e-13. The frame gives the bits of
    the F-341 frame for the plain form and without motion. The F-341, F-331 and F-340 tests, the F-258 bit records and
    baseline_hashes pass unedited, and five mutations were caught. One amendment: the first closed-form check excluded
    too few boundary cells (8.9e-3); it was diagnosed and replaced on a longer grid. Limits: the lab memory is derived
    for translation along a planar layer; matched forms on rotating meshes are not built; library only; two-dimensional
    checks. STATUS recorded PARTIAL by the lead: the registered check G3 missed (a defect of its set-up, 8.92e-3 against
    1e-12) and passed only as G3b after amendment 1, which is not blind to the scratch model that explained the miss;

  - note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). Size M. Stub ADR 0319; the registration is

  - depends on: F-408, F-399

- [~] **F-419** Three-node shell element (flat facet, assumed shear strain) for triangulated surfaces
  - depends on: F-408, F-391, F-392

    each other for the two diagonal directions. Cantilever strip, nu = 0: tip deflection within 1 percent. Pinched ring

    internal pressure: radial displacement p R^2/(E t) within 1 percent. First frequency of the simply supported plate
    within 2 percent. A free plate has six zero frequencies below 1e-6 of the seventh; a single element has exactly six
    zero eigenvalues; a triangle with an angle below the registered limit is refused with the element.
  - note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310). F-419 (ADR 0454, 2026-11-14): Shell3, a three-node flat
    shell for triangulated surfaces: CST membrane, Reissner-Mindlin bending, MITC3 shear with the Lyly-Stenberg-Vihinen
    stabilisation (alpha 0.1, longest edge), Shell4's drilling penalty, consistent mass with rotary inertia; pressure,
    gravity, centrifugal, nodal body force and thermal loads, centroid stresses, VTK_TRIANGLE output. Patch tests to
    1e-13, SS plate 0.998 and 0.997 of Navier at t/a 0.01 and 0.001 (plain MITC3 locks at 0.899), cantilever 0.99986,
    pinched ring 0.9991, cylinder within 1.8e-3, free plates six zero modes; models without Shell3 bit-identical.
    Partial: the .vtu check met only after amendment 1 added the triangle cell to rcfd_io::vtk. The one-diagonal
    cylinder O1 is diagnosed and met by the opt-in angle-weighted pressure of F-540 (ADR 0461). Follow-ups F-539, F-540
    (done, ADR 0461), F-541.

  - depends on: F-419, F-391, F-392, F-395, F-396

- [~] **F-421** Aerodynamic damping and added mass of a mode by prescribed motion of the wall (energy method)
  - depends on: F-408, F-362, F-383, F-400, F-401
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Force harmonics: for a synthetic
    force history with known in-phase and quadrature parts the extraction returns them within 1e-10, and the work per
    cycle equals pi q0 times the quadrature part within 1e-10. Piston on a column of incompressible fluid with an open
    end (the case of F-401): added mass rho_f A L_f within 2 percent and a damping ratio below the registered viscous
    and time-step estimate. Piston driving a plane channel of gap h and length L_f: force per piston velocity equal to A
    times the oscillating-channel impedance i w rho L_f/(1 - tanh(kappa)/kappa), kappa = (h/2) sqrt(i w/nu), real and
    imaginary parts within 3 percent at Womersley numbers 1 and 5 after the registered extrapolation in the time step,
    and the low-frequency limit 12 mu L_f/h^2 within 3 percent. The damping ratio of the bar on the open column from
    this method and from the decay of the coupled run of F-401 are both recorded. A history that has not become periodic
    within the registered tolerance is refused with the cycle-to-cycle change.
  - note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310). PARTIAL (ADR 0446, 2026-11-14; registered before the code,
    amendments 1 to 3 after registered runs). rcfd_post::solid_aerodamp: drive_mode moves the wall of a cosim::Fluid in
    a mode shape through an InterfaceMap (q = q0 sin(w t)) and records the generalised force by the transposed map;
    Harmonic::fit (least squares of mean, sine and cosine), periodic_response (every cycle fitted; refused with the
    cycle-to-cycle change of the first harmonic above a tolerance), added mass Q_p/(w^2 q0), damping -Q_q/(w q0),
    impedance, work per cycle pi q0 Q_q, damping ratio -W/(2 pi w^2 q0^2 m). Synthetic history: in-phase and quadrature
    parts to 4.8e-16, work per cycle against pi q0 Q_q to 4.0e-16, a decaying history refused naming the change (after
    amendment 1: the test's parse of the message). F-401's open column at T/100: added mass 0.997698 rho_f A L_f (limit
    2 percent), damping ratio 3.14582e-2 against the registered tan(w dt)/2 + 1e-4 (the step's lag; viscous part
    8.8e-7). Plane channel (h = 0.02 m, L_f = 100 h), the roadmap's impedance A i w rho L_f/(1 - tanh(kappa)/kappa)
    verified by derivation (12 mu L_f/h^2 is the limit per unit piston area): after the Richardson extrapolation in the
    time step, real and imaginary parts within 8.3e-3 and 1.6e-3 at Womersley 5, 3.2e-3 and 7.3e-3 at Womersley 1, the
    low-frequency limit within 9.8e-3; but only after amendments: the registered Womersley-5 run missed the real part by
    8.5e-2 (the Symmetry planes of the one-cell 2D reduction add dissipation, about 7 percent; corrected with
    zero-gradient planes), and the registered Womersley-1 and low-frequency runs diverged (the PISO step is unstable
    above nu dt/dy^2 of about 3.5, also on a fixed mesh; corrected with fewer cells across and more steps). Bar on the
    open column: damping ratio 1.756e-2 (ratio 0.5) and 2.896e-2 (ratio 4) by this method, 1.777e-2 and 2.889e-2 from
    the decay of F-401's coupled run (agreement 1.2e-2, 2.5e-3): the lag of the pairing. Partial: the W5 miss, the
    amendments, and the order companion of the Womersley-1 imaginary part (0.68, limit 0.8). Seven mutations caught. No
    line of rcfd-fv or rcfd-api changed. Open: ADR 0446 Q1 to Q3. Follow-ups F-530 (PISO stability at large diffusion
    numbers), F-531 (Symmetry viscous flux). F-530 (ADR 0451, 2026-11-14): the divergence is the corrector instability
    of ADR 0214; with the consistent correctors and 8 outer iterations the Womersley-1 piston channel of this item (40
    cells across) runs at nu dt/dy^2 = 25 and 50 and matches the impedance within 0.46 and 0.32 percent after the
    extrapolation. ADR 0455 (F-531, 2026-11-14): the Symmetry-plane dissipation of amendment 3 is the averaged component
    diagonal of the PISO correctors; with the opt-in corrected diagonal the registered W5 set-up (Symmetry planes) gives
    8.3e-3 and 1.6e-3 against the formula, equal to W5c to 2.4e-6.

  - depends on: F-408, F-389, F-397

    + (E H/(E + H)) (eps - sigma_y/E) within 1e-10 in one step and in 100; on reversal the bar yields again at
    -sigma_max with isotropic and at sigma_max - 2 sigma_y with kinematic hardening within 1e-10. Thick sphere b/a = 2,
    perfectly plastic, internal pressure: the pressure at plastic radius c equals 2 sigma_y ln(c/a) + (2 sigma_y/3)(1 -
    c^3/b^3) within 1 percent at c = 1.25 a and 1.5 a, the solve converges at 0.98 of the limit pressure 2 sigma_y
    ln(b/a), and the residual hoop stress at the bore after unloading equals the closed form within 2 percent. Beam of
    rectangular section in pure bending: M/M_y = 1.5 - 0.5 (kappa_y/kappa)^2 within 1 percent up to kappa = 5 kappa_y.
    The last three residuals of each step show an order >= 1.8; a halved step restores the state bit for bit; a
    non-positive yield stress and a softening curve are refused with the key.

  - depends on: F-408, F-391, F-392, F-393, F-394
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. With matching meshes the tied model
    equals the merged one within 1e-10. Flat non-matching interfaces 2:3 and 3:5 under uniaxial stress: far-end
    displacement within 0.1 percent and interface stress within the registered 3 percent (a one-sided node-to-surface
    tie does not pass the patch test exactly), the error falling with an observed order >= 1 under refinement. A
    cantilever cut in two and tied 2:3 (Tet10 to Hex20): tip deflection within 1 percent of the closed form. The
    constraint forces of a tie have zero resultant and moment within 1e-10. A node farther from every face than the
    registered tolerance is refused with its id. Joints: a beam continuing a solid bar and a shell continuing a solid
    plate give the tip deflection of the one-piece cantilever within 1 and 2 percent. Cyclic: the ring sector of F-394
    with a 2:3 boundary has its frequencies within 0.5 percent of the matching sector; a solid disc with nodes on the
    axis, spinning (index 0): centre stress (3 + nu) rho Omega^2 b^2/8 within 1 percent; a rod on the axis at index 1
    has the bending frequency of the beam within 1 percent, and at index 2 its axis nodes are held.
  - note: Structural solver, advanced tier (plan ADR 0310, 2026-11-12). ADR 0456, 2026-11-14: rcfd_fem::tie,
    node-to-surface ties (bucket grid, Gauss-Newton projection on Tri3/Quad4/Tri6/Quad8 faces, refusal FemError::TieGap
    with the node id above 0.05 of the mean master face size) and segment-integrated mortar ties (Sutherland-Hodgman
    clipping in the slave face plane, collapsed 4 x 4 Gauss, u_s = D^-1 M u_m per component with prescribed slave

    and shell_to_solid least-squares rigid couplings in solved form; Constraint::cyclic_with with CyclicOptions
    (interpolated non-matching boundaries by either tie, nodes on the axis by the null space of their own harmonic
    rows). Met: matching meshes tied equal merged 4.1e-14; flat 2:3 and 3:5 interfaces under uniaxial stress with the
    mortar tie exact to 2.8e-12 (displacement) and 5.8e-10 (stress), the node-to-surface tie within 4e-11 of an
    independent numpy prototype (far-end error 2.9e-3 at 2:3 falling with order 1.014, local stress error 0.149 not
    falling: the roadmap's 3 percent and falling stress hold for the mortar tie only); cantilever Tet10 to Hex20 tied
    2:3 within 5.8e-5 (mortar) and 8.4e-5 (NTS); tie constraint forces' resultant and moment 3.3e-13; ring sector with a
    2:3 boundary within 3.9e-3 of the matching sector; spinning disc with axis nodes, centre stress field within 1.0e-3;
    rod on the axis at index 1 within 4.2e-3 of the Timoshenko beam (after an amendment of the modal tolerance), axis
    nodes held at index 2. Missed: beam continuing a solid bar 2.25 percent (limit 1), shell continuing a solid plate
    2.36 percent (limit 2): the unit-weight couplings on Quad8 faces and the corner-column search are too flexible (a
    rigid face gives 9e-6); known-miss records. Eleven mutations caught. Default bits unchanged (B1, baseline_hashes).

    2026-11-14): the consistent and rigid joint couplings meet J1 (5.4e-6) and J2 (5.6e-4); the unit-weight couplings
    and their known-miss records are kept unchanged.

  - depends on: F-348

    coarsen along axes C, the smallest dyadic ancestor box (levels lowered only along C) that is exactly tiled by leaves
    of the mesh, each marked along every axis on which it is coarsened, is merged into one leaf with the levels of the
    box; with balance the merge is accepted only if the new leaf stays within one level of its face neighbours along
    every refined axis; the transfer is the existing Merged source (volume-weighted mean, so sum V q is conserved and

    state, 24 random sequences of splits, pair merges and box merges, 6 of them pair-stuck) return to the base in at

    balance refuse the registered cases. adapt (Coarsening::Pair) is unchanged: equal to adapt_with(.., Pair) bit for

    under rcfd-cosim/1 (cosim_case::host). On the model problem of ADR 0256 written as a case, with the mock structure
    of ADR 0345 in a third process and the unchanged coupled_step driving both over TCP: all 650 steps converged (7 to
    10 iterations, mean 8.766, last test 9.995e-9), omega_m/omega 0.998618 and 1.011453, and the displacements of every
    node at every step equal to the in-process run of the same case bit for bit (limit 1e-12 X; the case also equals the
    hand-built CWs bit for bit over 100 steps); a structure stiffer by 1e-9 is seen (4.15e-9 X). Structure::elements (a
    provided method, empty by default) is carried by cosim.describe only when not empty and returned by
    RemoteStructure::elements, so InterfaceMap::build runs on the coupler's side with the bits of the in-process build.
    service::Client writes each request with one call (unit-tested; 0.047 ms per call). Without the table every case
    hash, written case text and baseline hash is unchanged and the MCP goldens pass unedited; the schema gains the
    optional property cosim and the help of serve gains [--cosim <case>], both awaiting the maintainer's approval (ADR
    0380 Q1). Seven of eight mutations caught; treating fixed_patches as sliding is not seen by this model problem (its
    wall moves along x only, so a sliding and a fixed xmax give the same mesh; Q3). Not delivered: a structure from a
    case, the participant's own name (always fluid, Q2), more than one participant per rcfd serve, models other than the
    incompressible flow. Open: ADR 0380 Q1 to Q4. ADR 0381 (2026-11-13, F-481): MU5 is now caught by a tangential wall
    displacement; F-444 stays partial for the schema and serve help approval (ADR 0380 Q1).
- [~] **F-445** Overset: prescribed flux on the faces between calculated and fringe cells
  - depends on: F-349, F-344
  - acceptance: An opt-in of the overset step under which the flux of a face between a calculated and a fringe cell is
    the face interpolation of the interpolated fringe velocity plus one correction per closed fringe ring that makes the
    net flux of each enclosed part zero (ADR 0340, the switch described there): on RE of ADR 0340 at levels 1 to 3 the
    following coefficient a_c at both fringes is at least 0.9 at t = 0.025 and the order of R_b at t = 0.5 is at least
    1.7 on both pairs, on RL the order of R_b is at least 1.7 within the parity families (levels 1 to 3 and 2 to 4),
    continuity of the calculated cells and the mass of the domain hold to 1e-9, the uniform-flow check U1 of ADR 0219
    holds, and without the opt-in every overset result is bit-identical; or the ADR shows with a number why the
    prescribed flux is not admissible.
  - note: From ADR 0340 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR
    0347, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. Built as an opt-in of the overset solver, OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux, default off,
    every result without it bit-identical (state hashes of two runs equal to those of the library before,
    baseline_hashes and the twelve existing overset test files pass unedited). The flux of a face between a calculated
    and a fringe cell is the face interpolation of the velocity each pressure corrector starts from plus one correction
    per region of calculated cells that makes its net flux zero (it replaces the offset of the background fringe
    pressures). The switch as ADR 0340 words it (variant P, the interpolated fringe pressure left in the Green-Gauss
    gradient of the calculated cells next to the fringe) is not admissible: the Taylor-Green run on RE blows up at step
    5 (level 1) and step 3 (level 2), the error growing 11-fold and 60-fold per step, as predicted before the run from
    the pressure mismatch of the two parts (growth with the refinement). With that gradient taken from the own part
    (variant G, FringeFlux::PrescribedOwnGradient) it is stable: continuity 4.5e-13, flux through the hole ring 1.9e-14,
    U1 3.6e-15, a uniformly accelerating flow exact to 2e-15, the flux of a ring face equal to the mean of the two cell
    velocities to 4e-4. Order of R_b at t = 0.5 on RE 1.962, 1.789 (default coupling 0.983, 1.015); on RL within the
    parity families 2.704 (levels 1 to 3) and 2.124 (2 to 4); the response per unit of truncation is 1.51, 1.54, 1.65 at
    levels 1 to 3 (default 0.168, 0.339, 0.497). Missed: a_c at t = 0.025 is 0.598, 0.856, 0.931 at the background
    fringe and 0.867, 1.037, 1.053 at the component fringe against 0.9 (levels 1 and 2 miss); diagnosed as the decay of
    the answer of the calculated cells over one cell (the dipole estimate made before the run gave 0.65 at level 1), not
    a softness of the imposition; it rises to 0.906, 0.968, 0.989 by t = 0.5. Found on the way, registered checks missed
    and kept as known misses: under G the interpolation error reaches the calculated cells in full, so the velocity
    error against the exact solution on RE is 1.77, 1.64, 1.62 times that of the default coupling (limit 1.5) and R_b
    itself is 9.0, 4.6, 3.3 times the default's; with the quadratic donor interpolation of F-336 on both fringes the
    error of G falls to 0.63, 0.60, 0.56 of that and is 1.145, 1.056, 1.035 times the default's (hypothesis confirmed by
    its registered numbers). Not a candidate for a default. One unit check missed by round-off of its own test values
    (2.0e-12 against 1e-12) and was corrected by an amendment before the corrected run. Seven mutations caught. Not
    covered: accuracy with a moving component, RL at level 5, the combination with the other overset opt-ins beyond a
    smoke check. ADR 0376 (F-450), 2026-11-12: G runs with the moving, turning component of ADR 0219 without a fault
    (TG_1 and TG_2, quadratic stencils, continuity 6e-13, no refusal); the motion does not add to its excess over the
    default coupling, which sits in the calculated background cells next to the background fringe (the one-sided
    gradient of D5).
