- [~] **F-447** Electron over the rcfd APIs: performance spike (control, live events, field transfer, scrubbing, WebGPU draw)
  - acceptance: The checks P1 to P12 of ADR 0350 are run once as registered on the maintainer's machine, with the
    rcfd-studio control column measured first; each bulk route (R0 JSON baseline, R1 binary side channel under an opt-in
    data.* method family of protocol 1.2, R2 a TypeScript reader of store.rts, R3 a WebAssembly reader if it needs no
    new crate) is recorded; the negative controls NC1 and NC2 hold; the decision of ADR 0350 section 4 (viable, viable
    with conditions, not viable) is stated with the numbers; no existing service method, golden or hash changes.
  - note: ADR 0350 (2026-11-12), asked for by the maintainer. Q1 (run the spike) answered by the maintainer in person on
    2026-11-12; Q2 to Q5 taken with the recommendations (ADR 0350 decision record). ADR 0350, 2026-11-12. The Electron
    spike ran once on the maintainer's machine (Electron 45.1.0, RTX 5080, 60 Hz display, load 0.3 to 0.6). Bulk data is
    fast enough and exact by both routes: R1 (the opt-in `data.*` methods, `rcfd-data/1`, service protocol 1.2, raw
    `f32` on a second TCP connection) loads a 1e6-cell scalar to a GPU buffer in p50 25.9 ms, p99 57.7 ms; R2 (a reader
    of `store.rts` in Node) in p50 14.2 ms, p99 22.4 ms; JSON (R0) takes 552 ms. Scrubbing 30.8 and 60.1 snapshots per s
    at 1e6 cells, 10.5 and 17.8 at 4e6; first picture of the 1e6 surface 1.15 s (R1, first opening 1.58 s) and 0.06 s
    (R2); 1e6 triangles at 332 frames per s without a rate limit and p99 16.9 ms per frame with vertical sync; cold
    start median 0.38 s (one start of ten took 6.7 s); renderer memory 112 MB with 20 snapshots; 0 differing bits in
    672e6 values; service round trip p50 0.06 ms; event latency p99 under 2.1 ms. Missed: P3, `monitors.get` of 4 series
    of 1e5 samples takes 127 ms against 100 ms (a 12 MB reply, most of the time on the service's side). R3 (WebAssembly)
    not run: it needs `unsafe` exports or `wasm-bindgen`. The rcfd-studio control, offscreen: 12.7 ms per snapshot, 73
    per s, first picture 1.25 s. The registered rule has no outcome for a miss of P3 alone, so viability is the
    maintainer's decision; questions QA1 to QA5 of addendum 1. P3 is met after F-456 (ADR 0353, 2026-11-12): median 82.6
    ms against 100; viability remains the maintainer's decision.

- [~] **F-450** Overset: the prescribed fringe flux with a moving component
  - depends on: F-445, F-336
  - acceptance: With OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux(PrescribedOwnGradient) and the quadratic donor interpolation of
    F-336, the Taylor-Green set-up of ADR 0219 with the moving, turning component (levels 1 and 2, the corrected time
    step of its amendment 2) is run against the default coupling with the same stencils: the largest velocity error over
    the calculated and fringe cells is at most 1.2 times that of the default coupling at both levels, continuity and the
    outflow balance hold to 1e-9 in every step, and no step is refused for a calculated cell between fringe cells on
    opposite sides; or the ADR names with a number what the moving fringe adds (the lag of the prescribed flux on the
    faces that change kind is the first candidate).
  - note: From ADR 0347 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR
    0376, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL. No library change: OversetSolver::set_fringe_flux(PrescribedOwnGradient) runs with the
    moving, turning component as it stands. On TG_L of ADR 0219 with the quadratic donor interpolation on both runs and
    dt proportional to h^2 (200 and 800 steps), every step is taken (no refusal of a cell between fringe cells, no
    unconverged solve, no fallback), continuity 1.6e-13 and 6.2e-13, the flux into the hole region 3.8e-15 and 8.9e-15
    and through the domain boundary 0, 142 and 503 kind changes. The largest error over the calculated and fringe cells
    is 1.2636 times that of the default coupling at level 1 (9.7081e-4 against 7.6831e-4; limit 1.2, missed, kept as a
    known miss) and 1.0001 at level 2 (both in the domain-boundary cell); the order of the error of G is 2.33. What the
    moving fringe adds, measured against the same runs with the component at rest: nothing; the excess of G over the
    default on the overlap is 1.21 and 1.06 moving against 1.43 and 1.10 at rest (m_G / m_default 0.844, 0.965), so the
    lag on the faces that change kind does not show. The excess is local to the calculated background cells within two
    cells of the background fringe (1.93 and 1.52 times the default there; elsewhere equal within 4 percent; the
    hypothesis as registered after the first run is ruled out by its deciding numbers, its maximum leaving the band at
    level 2), the one-sided pressure gradient of the ring cells of ADR 0347 D5. The root mean square error of each class
    is that of the default within 1.1 percent or smaller. Defaults untouched (two hashes equal to the library before,
    baseline_hashes and the existing overset tests pass). Four mutations: three caught by their checks, the fourth (the
    flux taken relative to the moving faces) seen only by the number of the check that already misses (1.59e4). Open:
    whether the alternative clause of the acceptance makes it done (ADR 0376 Q1). ADR 0409 (F-479), 2026-11-13: with the
    second-order ring gradient opt-in, the excess of G in the background band falls from 1.93 and 1.52 to 0.89 and 1.02
    times the default coupling, and e_max(G) / e_max(default) at level 1 from 1.2636 to 1.0000.

- [x] **F-452** Wave solver driven by a sampled CFD surface
  - depends on: F-333
  - acceptance: A driven boundary built from an rcfd-surface-series file reproduces, in a duct, the modal amplitudes of
    a closed-form duct field sampled into that file within 1 percent; a series that does not cover a whole number of
    periods is refused.
  - note: From ADR 0351 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE
    pending acceptance, ADR 0372, 2026-11-12. Library only. Built: rcfd-post `wave_drive.rs` (`SurfaceDrive`,
    `DuctFrame`, `DriveOptions`): an rcfd-surface-series section is read as a whole number of periods of a given
    fundamental, each harmonic of every face taken by a DFT on the file's clock (the mean dropped and reported), fitted
    on a hard-walled duct-mode basis, and played back periodically as the `WaveBc::Driven` ghost state of the wave
    entering the duct, each mode with its own axial wavenumber and impedance kz p/(rho0 omega), carried from the
    sampling plane to the driven faces. Registered checks, all met at the first run, no amendment: a 0.12 m channel, a
    closed-form field of the plane wave at 1181 Hz and the plane wave and mode 1 at 2361 Hz plus a 3 Pa mean, sampled on
    a wall-clustered 24-face section 0.02 m upstream of the wave mesh into the file through JSON text; on 64 cells
    across the amplitudes measured at the inlet agree with the closed form within 8.8e-4, 3.5e-3 and 2.3e-3 (limit 1e-2;
    1.4e-2 at worst on 32 across, second order: the error is the scheme's driven face, the file chain adds 1.1e-14
    against a run driven by the closed form); the drive's state equals the closed form within 1.7e-13; a 128-sample
    two-period file is accepted and 127 and 96 samples are refused as not a whole number of periods; eleven other
    refusals located. Six mutations caught (plane-wave impedance, lost file clock, period test removed, wrong axial
    carry, harmonics played at the fundamental, Nyquist test removed). Limits: the sampled pressure must be the entering
    wave only; periodic signals; static section, medium at rest; only the two-dimensional channel was run; no case key
    or CLI (F-451). The returning-wave limit is lifted for two or more sampled sections by F-478 (ADR 0378, 2026-11-12);
    since then the off-plane refusal names the farthest face.
- [~] **F-453** Circular and three-dimensional ducts through the wave solver
  - depends on: F-333
  - acceptance: A spinning mode (1, 0) and a radial mode (0, 1) of a hard-walled circular duct on an O-grid propagate
    with the closed-form axial wavenumber within 1 percent after the polygonal cut-off error of the grid, estimated in
    the registration, is accounted for; a matched layer ends the duct with less than 1 percent reflection.
  - note: PARTIAL, ADR 0366, 2026-11-12. Library only. The acceptance clauses are met; two registered checks missed and
    one registered mutation escaped its registered check, so the item is partial by Rule I. Built: rcfd-mesh
    `circular_duct_ogrid` (an O-grid of a circular duct: an n x n core and four n x n/2 ring blocks, extruded along z;
    patches wall, inlet, outlet), and tests that drive the duct through the F-333 `AcousticWaveSolver` and measure it
    with `duct_modes`. Radius 0.06 m, each mode at cos theta = 0.8, matched layer one axial wavelength thick before a
    rigid end. The spinning mode (1, 0) at 2768 Hz on n = 16 (110 k cells) has an axial wavenumber 2.58e-3 below the
    closed form corrected for the 64-sided polygon (the correction is the equal-area radius, first-order Hadamard,
    -4.5e-4; 3.03e-3 below the circle's form); the layer reflects 3.6e-5. The radial mode (0, 1) at 5760 Hz on n = 32
    (424 k cells) is 2.56e-3 below (correction -1.1e-4); reflection 6.5e-5. Both match a Fourier analysis of the scheme
    within about 5 percent. The Bessel zeros are computed in the test from the power series and agree with the library
    within 1.1e-14. Coarse covering runs met their limits, and the rigid end without a layer reflects 0.9995. Missed:
    the counter-rotating (-1, 0) content of the spinning runs is 1.2e-5 against a registered 1e-6 (estimate
    "round-off"). Diagnosed (amendment 1): the solver commutes with the grid's rotation to 1e-15, and the content falls
    in a longer run, so it is left over from the start-up ramp of the drive. Mutation MU3 (wall given the open flux)
    escaped the registered conservation check U8, whose initial field has a zero boundary mean; four duct checks caught
    it. Limits: two modes at one frequency each, one O-grid topology, no rectangular 3-D duct, one planar layer, medium
    at rest; no case key or CLI (ADR 0351 question 1, F-451). The blind spot of U8 (mutation MU3 escaping with a
    zero-boundary-mean field) is closed by F-473 (ADR 0371, 2026-11-12), whose closed-duct check with a non-zero
    boundary mean catches it.
- [~] **F-454** Fractional step: a step-consistent face flux for the projection
  - depends on: F-443
  - acceptance: The steady lid-driven cavity of ADR 0245 C3 with solver.time_advance = "fractional_step" (8.7e-2 between
    dt = 0.04 and 0.01, ADR 0352 F0) is traced to its face term with a number, and either made the same to 1e-9 for the
    two step sizes by an opt-in (defaults bit-identical) or the ADR names why not with a number.
  - note: From ADR 0352 question 2, recommendation (a). ADR 0356, 2026-11-12: PARTIAL by the rule (every acceptance
    clause met; mutation MF5 equivalent by construction, not caught). The fractional step's 8.69e-2 between dt 0.04 and
    0.01 is its face term: in a steady state the increment vanishes, the cell equations carry no step, and the face
    defect is dte R(p) (measured to 6.5e-16 relative), a first-order pressure smoothing. The opt-in
    PimpleSettings::fractional_step_consistent (incremental form; default false) takes on internal faces Gamma R(p^n) +
    (Gamma/dt)(c1 d^n - c2 d^{n-1}) with Gamma the harmonic face value of V/a_P of the predictor, so the steady defect
    is R(p)/interp(a): the steady cavity is then the same to 1.5e-13 for the two steps (1.2e-13 with the plain boundary,
    1.1e-13 with BDF2, printed) and equal to the PISO step's with ADR 0245's C to 1.6e-13 (4.4e-2 without). Defaults bit
    for bit (fingerprints before and after equal; the rcfd-fv suites touching the changed lines and baseline_hashes
    unedited). The Chorin form is not changed (its cell equations carry dt; 3.7e-2 printed). No case key; outlets and
    periodic faces keep dte R. Four of five mutations caught. Partial by the registered rule; done is the maintainer's
    call; making the opt-in the default (Q3) is the maintainer's.
- [~] **F-455** Residual of the direct static solve on slender models, and iterative refinement
  - depends on: F-374, F-376
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The relative residual of the
    default direct static solve is recorded for Tet4, Hex8 and Tet10 cantilevers of slenderness 5, 10, 20 and 40 at
    registered meshes; with one step of iterative refinement (opt-in, the default bit-identical) the relative residual
    is at most 1e-14 on every one of them and the strain energy equals half the work of the loads within 1e-12; the cost
    of the refinement step is recorded.
  - note: ADR 0397, 2026-11-13: rcfd_fem::refine (two_sum, two_product by fma, Dot2 of Ogita-Rump-Oishi,
    residual_compensated, refine_step, residual_statistics with rho_w, rho_x, phi_w = eps |||K||u|||/||f||, phi_rep =
    (u/sqrt 3) ||(sum_j k_ij^2 u_j^2)^(1/2)||/||f|| and omega = ||r||/(|||K||u||| + ||f||), energy_defect) and
    StaticOptions::refinement(steps) (direct solve and plain path only, solver name skyline-ldlt-refined; default
    bit-identical, digest b9d9056b0c5a7aff of the twelve default solves equal on main and branch). Twelve cantilevers
    (Tet4, Hex8, Tet10; section 0.2 m with 2 x 2 cells; L/h = 5, 10, 20, 40): default relative residual 5.9e-13 to
    8.0e-9, at 0.29 to 0.42 of the evaluation floor phi_w; default backward error omega <= 7.4e-17 (the direct solve is
    backward stable). One refinement step with the compensated residual: true relative residual 2.1e-13 to 1.8e-9, at
    0.61 to 1.15 of the representability floor of any double vector; omega 1.4e-17 to 3.3e-17; energy of the stored
    stiffness against half the work 7e-19 to 4e-17 (default up to 8e-10); a second step changes nothing; the step costs
    0.036 to 0.055 of factor and solve. The 1e-14 relative residual is below the floor on all twelve (registered
    expected miss, derived before the run); the recovered strain energy (ADR 0277's W1) misses 1e-12 on nine cases at
    1.6e-12 to 7.1e-10 because the recovery, the element matrices and the assembled stiffness are three roundings of one
    operator whose energies differ by 0.01 to 0.3 phi_w on near-rigid displacements (ADR 0277's 2.6e-12 and 1.5e-11 are
    this floor, not the solve's residual). Open: re-word the residual clause to omega <= 1e-14 and rho_x <= 2 phi_rep,
    and read the strain energy as that of the stored stiffness (both met). Open for the maintainer (ADR 0397 questions 1
    and 2): the proposed re-worded acceptance in the ADR (backward error and twice the rounding floor; strain energy as
    half u^T K u of the assembled stiffness), which the measured numbers meet.

    build_second_order_bounded (dt 1e-3) was reproduced from t = 0 (the printed coefficients and the message of ADR 0268
    R1 exactly) and from a state written to disk at step 2900 (the same stop, every Courant number bit-equal); the flow
    is healthy one step before (Courant 1.136, max |u| 0.995 of step 2000). Located by an opt-in capture of the pressure
    systems (PimpleSolver::pressure_capture, replayed bit for bit with pressure::pressure_system_src) and a read-only
    AMG trace: in corrector 1 of step 2951 the inputs are finite, the matrix is a symmetric M-matrix and the volume
    source of the solid cells is finite and balanced (sum 1e-15 of its maximum, the same size as at steps 2949 and
    2950), but the AMG-preconditioned CG has r^T z < 0 from its first iteration, stagnates and overflows (beta not
    finite at iteration 801), so the whole pressure is NaN; cell 0 at the inlet corner is only the first index of an
    all-NaN vector. Incomplete-Cholesky CG solves the same system in 448 iterations. The stop is a breakdown of the
    linear solver, not of the forcing. Delivered (opt-in, defaults bit-identical, baseline_hashes pass):
    PimpleSettings::pressure_ic_fallback repeats a non-finite pressure solve with IC-CG from the same start and records
    it in PimpleSolver::pressure_fallbacks. With it T runs to t = 8 with one repeat in 5050 steps (S2 held, 7
    crossings): max C_D 3.22695 (+0.216 percent), max C_L 1.00253 (+1.687 percent), St 0.30144 (-0.146 percent), so
    A2-T-2 of ADR 0268 is met (0.216 to 0.136, 1.687 to 0.175). Nine mutations caught. Open (ADR 0363 Q4 to Q6): why the
    AMG hierarchy loses definiteness on this system, making the repeat the default, a guard on rz <= 0 inside cg. ADR
    0369 (2026-11-12, F-474): the AMG breakdown at step 2951 is the coarsest dense LU order defect (F-471); with
    AmgSettings::coarse_lu_interchanges_first the stopping system converges in 10 iterations and T does not stop.

- [~] **F-471** Scalar AMG coarsest dense LU: row interchanges applied before the forward substitution
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. A test shows whether the coarsest
    dense LU of rcfd_linalg::amg (DenseLu) interchanges rows on each fluid case of the baseline set and records where;
    DenseLu::solve applies every interchange before the forward substitution (as rcfd_linalg::amg_elastic after ADR 0305
    amendment 1) so that a coarsest matrix that needs interchanges is solved to a relative residual of 1e-12; the
    rcfd-linalg, rcfd-fv and rcfd-api tests and the baseline hashes are run, and any changed hash is reported to the
    maintainer, not re-recorded.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0369, 2026-11-12, with F-474). The defect is shown in rcfd_linalg::amg DenseLu: whole-row swaps
    in the factorisation with interleaved interchanges in the solve give (-13, 15, -5) for (1, 1, 1) on a 3 x 3 SPD
    matrix, a relative residual of 4e-3 on a 20 x 20 SPD tridiagonal, and 0.21 on the coarsest operator of the T
    pressure system of ADR 0363, where it is the cause of the AMG-CG breakdown (F-474). Interchanges at step 0 alone are
    harmless. On the baseline set only kepsilon_channel (coarsest 56) and cavity-coupled (Schur, coarsest 71) reach an
    AMG, and neither interchanges (scratch instrumentation). The corrected order is built as the opt-in
    AmgSettings::coarse_lu_interchanges_first (5e-15 and 9e-19 relative residual). With it as the default on a scratch
    copy, baseline_hashes, case_hashes_w48u, rcfd-linalg (except ADR 0369 L1, which pins the old default), rcfd-fv lib
    and the defaults tests f301/f367 pass, so no registered hash moves; the T bounded run of ADR 0268/0363 changes (no
    stop, different from step 2917). Remaining (NEEDS THE USER): switch the default and run the AMG-using
    rcfd-fv/rcfd-api test files in the gate; ADR 0363's records H1, H2 and H3a and ADR 0369 L1 assert the old behaviour.
    NEEDS THE USER: switching the default (no registered hash moves; ADR 0363's stop records and ADR 0369 L1 would need
    new records).

  - depends on: F-453
  - acceptance: On the closed circular O-grid duct, an initial pressure with a non-zero mean on every patch keeps sum p

    closed circular O-grid duct (circular_duct_ogrid(6, 3, 6), 648 cells) the initial pressure p = 1 + 0.4 x/R + 0.3 y/R
    + 0.5 z/L has a mean of 1.25 on the wall, 1.04 on the inlet and 1.46 on the outlet. With every patch a wall, 100

    the integral by 0.955 and is caught by the closed check; a wall leak of 1e-9 is caught (7.8e-9 against 1e-12); an

- [~] **F-474** AMG pressure preconditioner: loss of definiteness on the immersed T system
  - depends on: F-466
  - acceptance: On the pressure system of ADR 0363 (T, bounded immersed forcing, step 2951 corrector 1, rebuilt from the
    state of step 2950 and the opt-in capture) the cause of r^T M^-1 r < 0 of the smoothed-aggregation AMG is located by
    a registered measurement (per level, the Rayleigh quotient of the cycle, the smoothed prolongator and the coarse
    operators against a higher-precision product), and either the AMG is repaired so that AMG-CG converges on that
    system with every registered hash unchanged, or the breakdown is detected inside cg (rz <= 0) and reported with a
    located message.
  - note: PARTIAL (ADR 0369, 2026-11-12). From ADR 0363 Q4/Q6. Cause located on the stopping system of ADR 0363 (T,
    bounded forcing, step 2951 corrector 1, rebuilt from the state of step 2940): it is the coarsest dense LU order
    defect of F-471. The coarsest operator (24 unknowns) interchanges rows at steps 13, 16 and 17; the default
    interleaved DenseLu::solve misses by a relative residual of 0.21; the cycle becomes non-symmetric (0.13 at the
    coarsest level, 4.2e-3 at the finest) and indefinite (negative Rayleigh quotients at levels 4 and 0), hence r^T M^-1
    r < 0. Everything else is sound against double-double: Galerkin products to 6e-16, every operator symmetric to 5e-16
    and positive definite, no zero prolongator column. Delivered (opt-in, defaults bit-identical, baseline_hashes pass):
    AmgSettings::coarse_lu_interchanges_first applies every interchange before the forward substitution; with it the
    coarse solve is exact to 5e-15, the cycle symmetric to 1e-15 and positive on every level, and AMG-CG converges on
    the stopping system in 10 iterations (corrector 0: 10 against 406), agreeing with IC-CG to 4e-9; read-only accessors
    Amg::coarse_interchanges, level_operator, level_prolongator, cycle_at, coarse_solve. With the default switched on a
    scratch copy no registered hash moves (kepsilon_channel and cavity-coupled, the only baseline cases with an AMG,
    never interchange), T no longer stops at 2951, and its run differs from ADR 0363 H1 from step 2917 on. Seven
    mutations caught. Partial by Rule I: the check L4 missed (the Laplacian's coarsest LU interchanges at step 0,
    harmless to the order) and was corrected by amendment 1. Open: switching the default (maintainer; recommended).

  - depends on: F-363

    taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. The whole step of DFG 2D-2 on M2 (u_n, u_n-1, p,
    phi_n, phi_n-1; 165296 unknowns) was linearised by central finite differences about early states, with the solves
    converged to 1e-12, and its outer spectrum computed by Arnoldi with 40 vectors and a complex Hessenberg QR written
    from first principles; the linearisation is valid (the map at zero is the step to the bit, linear to 2e-5, the
    history shift exact, known spectra found to round-off, the stop at step 34 reproduced). With two correctors and at
    dt 5e-4 every Ritz value lies inside the unit circle (largest 0.970 and 0.979; most negative -0.48 and -0.78, real).
    With one corrector at dt 1e-3 the bounded form carries the period-two mode (at step 15 a converged pair -1.103 +-
    0.346i, magnitude 1.156, and a real -1.073; the fluid part of the step a real -1.139; at step 10 a real -1.265; the
    magnitude matches the run's growth of about 1.15 per step), at the body (0.0025 to 0.011 from the surface, a first
    fluid cell at step 5), but it is not the dominant eigenvalue: pressure modes of the fluid four cells above the
    cylinder have eigenvalues of positive real part up to 1.93, and the first-order forcing, which runs, has them too
    (1.58) and a real -1.024. Partial by the registered rule: known misses E1 b to d (not real, not dominant, not at a
    first fluid cell at step 15), E4 (the run that runs has -1.024), and after amendment 1 S1 (those modes are not in
    the solid) and P3 c. Open (ADR 0392 Q2): the positive eigenvalues above one of the single corrector at dt 1e-3 in
    both forcings, by a linearisation of several steps along the trajectory and the channel without the cylinder.
    Follow-up F-494. ADR 0405 (2026-11-13, F-494): over ten steps along the trajectory the bounded form grows by 1.88
    per step and the first-order forcing, which runs, by 1.31 (1.12 over twenty); the one-step eigenvalues above one
    belong to the early state at the body (none in the channel without the cylinder at the same Courant number, none at
    step 100).

    eigenvalues at steps 16 and 20 are 1.010 and 1.008 and the ten-step growth 1.012 (first-order) and 1.057 (bounded)
    per step; the bounded form with one corrector runs 200 steps, so the modes and the stop belong to the ADR 0249 start

- [x] **F-499** Coriolis coupling of a rotating part: gyroscopic matrix, whirl modes and the Campbell table
  - depends on: F-396

    int rho N_a N_b [a x] is skew to rounding; the quadratic eigenproblem (K_eff - omega^2 M + i omega G) phi = 0 is
    solved by a symmetric linearisation; at Omega = 0 the frequencies are those of F-396; a point mass on an isotropic

    ADR 0411, 2026-11-13: the Coriolis matrix G = 2 Omega C (C skew bit for bit), whirl modes of (K_eff - omega^2 M + i
    omega G) phi = 0 by Meirovitch's symmetric linearisation (state form with M* = blockdiag(M, K_eff), skew G*) solved
    by a dense skew Householder reduction and the QL algorithm (cap 1500 reduced unknowns), the whirl number kappa =
    Im(phi^H C phi)/phi^H M phi giving forward and backward whirl, the Campbell table of F-396 with directions and
    crossings linear in Omega; point mass and cube on springs within 3.2e-13 of omega_0 -/+ Omega with kappa = +/-1; on
    a cyclic sector G enters index k as T_k^T blockdiag(G_s, G_s) T_k (the cos/sin coupling comes through the rows of
    T_k; ADR 0407 D1's remark superseded), the sector equals the full rotor's 252 whirl frequencies within 3e-13; speeds
    above the loss of stiffness of K_eff stay reported as a loss.

    1.767 at step 16 to 2e-4. From the projected start the first-order forcing has one-step eigenvalues 1.010 and 1.008
    at steps 16 and 20 (old 1.77, 1.91; registered limit 1.2), a negative-real pressure mode below the body, not the old

    field's flow through the cylinder by the registered rule, at a higher Courant number (1.25) than the old start's.
    The bounded form with one corrector runs 200 steps from the projected start (max abs(u) 2.208; from the ADR 0249
    start it stops at step 34), with ten-step growth 1.057 per step over steps 16 to 25 (old 1.881), a weak
    pure-pressure mode at the surface. Five mutations caught.

- [~] **F-505** Whirl modes above the loss of stiffness: gyroscopic stabilisation
  - depends on: F-499
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. At a speed where K_eff is not
    positive definite the whirl problem is solved by a non-symmetric eigensolver of the state matrix written from first
    principles; each speed is flagged stable (all frequencies real within a registered tolerance) or unstable with the
    growth rate; the point mass on isotropic springs gives Omega - omega_0 and Omega + omega_0 above omega_0 within 1e-8
    and is flagged stable; an anisotropic spring pair gives the closed-form unstable band between the two spring
    frequencies.
  - note: From ADR 0411 question 1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. ADR
    0416, 2026-11-13: whirl modes at any speed by the state matrix A = [[0, c I], [-K^/c, -G^]] of the mass-scaled
    gyroscopic problem, eigenvalues by Householder reduction to Hessenberg form and the Francis double-shift QR
    algorithm, mode vectors by inverse iteration on Q(s) = s^2 M + s G + K_eff; each speed flagged stable when max|Re s|
    <= 1e-8 max|s|, otherwise unstable with the growth rate max Re s (RotatingPart::whirl_state, whirl_stability with
    CSV, gyroscopic_state_eigen_dense); whirl_modes still reports such speeds as a loss. Isotropic point mass above
    omega_0: Omega - omega_0 and Omega + omega_0 within 3.3e-15 relative, both backward, flagged stable; cube on springs
    gyroscopically stabilised (two negative eigenvalues of K_eff, pair within 1.9e-12); anisotropic pair unstable
    exactly between the spring frequencies with the closed-form growth within 1.1e-14 of omega_0, band edges by
    bisection within 2.2e-15, the same band on the cube within 2.4e-12. Partial by the rule: the registered odd-index
    check on the cube rested on a wrong torsion estimate (the pre-stress cancels the spin softening on a rigid rotation
    about the axis; amendment 1, met on a corrected set-up after the run), and one planned mutation (sign of G in the
    state matrix) is equivalent by the symmetry of the spectrum.

- [~] **F-530** Stability of the non-iterated PISO step at large diffusion numbers
  - depends on: F-421
  - acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. The divergence of the PISO step
    above nu dt/dy^2 of about 3.5 found by ADR 0446 (a plane channel driven by an oscillating inflow on a fixed mesh) is
    located in the step and either removed, so that the same channel at nu dt/dy^2 = 25 and 100 stays bounded over 3
    periods and matches the oscillating-channel impedance as the stable runs do, or refused by the step with a message
    naming the diffusion number; the default results of every existing case stay bit-identical.
  - note: Numerics. PARTIAL (ADR 0451, 2026-11-14; registered before the code, amendment 1 after the registered runs).
    Located: the divergence of ADR 0446 is the corrector instability of ADR 0214 (the first corrector over-corrects a
    pressure error by about the cross-gap diffusion number, the second does not remove the Rhie-Chow part left in the
    cell velocity): on the fixed-mesh channel driven by an oscillating inflow (120 x 40 cells, Womersley 1) the default
    step alternates in sign every step, the twin-run radius of the step map is 9.13 per step at nu dt/dy^2 = 25 against
    the ADR 0073 estimate 9.40, the estimate crosses one between 2.5 and 3.0 and is 5.0 at 16 cells across at the same
    number; more correctors lower it, the Rhie-Chow time term and the grading play no part. Removed by the opt-in
    consistent correctors of ADR 0214: bounded over 3 periods at nu dt/dy^2 = 25, 50 and 100. Found: with one outer
    iteration the step does not converge the pressure at such numbers (each corrector removes a few percent of a smooth
    pressure error), and the impedance's imaginary part is 14 percent low at 50 and 3 percent low at 25 (also with 8
    correctors); with the consistent correctors and 8 outer iterations (no relaxation) every level matches the discrete
    implicit-Euler impedance within 0.6 percent, the extrapolation the oscillating-channel impedance within 0.61 and
    0.38 percent and the stable default runs within 0.23 percent; the moving piston of F-421 the same (0.46, 0.32
    percent). Partial: the registered estimate of the rate (16 cells) and growth measurement missed, the option alone
    missed the impedance and one periodicity tolerance (a slowly decaying numerical mode, 0.95 to 0.99 per step), and
    the match was met only after the amendment, with 8 outer iterations taken from a diagnosis. No library line changed
    (defaults bit-identical); six mutations caught; docs/dynamic-mesh.md. Open: ADR 0451 Q1 to Q3. Follow-ups F-535
    (opt-in refusal naming the diffusion number), F-536 (outer-iteration criterion).
